definition_zh: 彻底地；完全地；认真地；极其
definition_en: in a complete and careful way, with every part attended to, or to a very great degree
core_image: 把柜子从顶板擦到底板，每一格都擦过一遍
scene: 搬家前打扫空房，主人连门框顶端和窗轨凹槽都不放过。She went through the flat thoroughly before the new tenants arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 thoroughly 是「彻底地、无一遗漏地」（第 1 个义项：每个角落都处理到）；句意为新房客到来前她把公寓彻底收拾了一遍。

pos.zh: 彻底地；全面地；认真仔细地

forms.label: 原级（形容词 thoroughly 的形容词形式）

derivatives.zh: 由副词去掉后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「彻底的；全面的」
由形容词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「彻底；周密」
thorough 与 fare 的古老复合词，义为「大道；通路」

senses.title: In a complete and careful way
senses.definition: in a way that covers every part or detail, so that nothing is left out
senses.definitionCN: 以涵盖每个部分或细节、无所遗漏的方式
senses.example: The mechanic thoroughly checked the brakes before the car left the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 修理工在车出厂前把刹车彻底检查了一遍。
senses.why: The word is the adverb of thorough, the old twin of through: something done thoroughly has been carried all the way through.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 thorough 的副词，而 thorough 是 through 的古老孪生词：彻底做完的事，就是被一路走穿到底的事。

senses.title: With great care and attention
senses.titleCN: 认真仔细地；一丝不苟地
senses.definition: with careful attention to correctness and detail, of a way of working or thinking
senses.definitionCN: 指工作或思考方式认真细致、注重正确与细节
senses.example: You should read the contract thoroughly before signing it.
senses.exampleCN: 签字前你应该认真通读合同。
senses.why: Care walks the whole road: the adverb marks the walker who leaves no step untaken.
senses.whyCN: 用心要走过整条路：这个副词标记的是不肯省下任何一步的走法。

senses.title: To a very great degree
senses.definition: to a very great degree, especially with verbs of feeling and opinion
senses.definitionCN: 程度很高，尤与表示感受和看法的动词连用
senses.example: I thoroughly enjoyed the concert last night.
senses.exampleCN: 昨晚的音乐会我听得十分过瘾。
senses.why: Completeness slides from the task to the feeling: a pleasure that is complete is one felt thoroughly.
senses.whyCN: 「彻底」从任务滑到感受上：完整的快乐就是被彻底感受到的快乐。

senses.title: Utterly, in a bad sense
senses.titleCN: 完全地；十足地（多含贬义）
senses.definition: completely and absolutely, often before a negative judgement
senses.definitionCN: 完全地、绝对地，常用于否定评价之前
senses.example: The plan was thoroughly misguided from the start.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划从一开始就完全走错了方向。
senses.why: The same completeness can measure failure or folly: the depth of the error is what the adverb reports.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「彻底」也能衡量失败与愚蠢：这个副词报告的是错误的深度。

intro.en: Thoroughly is the adverb built on thorough, the adjective twin of through; the whole family goes back to one Germanic root for passing from one side to the other.
intro.cn: thoroughly 是建立在 thorough 之上的副词，而 thorough 是 through 的形容词孪生词；整个词族都源自同一个表示「从一侧到另一侧」的日耳曼词根。

items.en: The old root behind through meant from one side to the other, with an image of a door or passage being crossed.
items.cn: through 背后的古老词根意为「从一侧到另一侧」，带着「穿过门或通道」的意象。

items.en: Old English had the preposition and adverb for passing through, and a compound meaning going right through, hence complete.
items.cn: 古英语已有表示「穿过」的介词与副词，并有「直贯而过」的复合词，引申为完全。

items.en: Middle English split the spellings: through kept the motion job, thorough took the completeness job, and -ly made the adverb.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写分化：through 保留运动义，thorough 接管「彻底」义，加 -ly 构成副词。

items.en: From the sixteenth century onward, thoroughly settled as the standard adverb for complete and careful action.
items.cn: 自十六世纪起，thoroughly 固定为表示「彻底、细致」动作的标准副词。

items.en: Modern usage extends it to degree, as in thoroughly enjoy, where the sense is intensity rather than coverage.
items.cn: 现代用法把它扩展到程度，如 thoroughly enjoy，此时表示强度而非覆盖范围。

note.en: The first group lines up the spelling family around thorough; the second compares adverbs and adjectives of completeness and care.
note.cn: 第一组排开 thorough 周边的拼写家族；第二组比较表示彻底与用心的副词和形容词。

entries.definition: Complete and careful, with nothing left out; the adjective this adverb is built on.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底的；全面的（thoroughly 所依附的形容词）

entries.definition: From one side to the other; the motion twin that shares the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过；通过（与 thorough 同根的运动义孪生词）

entries.definition: In every part of a place or period; through plus out.
entries.definitionCN: 遍及；自始至终（through 与 out 复合）

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being complete and careful.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「彻底、周密」，由 thorough 加 -ness 构成

entries.definition: In every part; the most general adverb of wholeness, with no image of care.
entries.definitionCN: 完全地（最一般的「完整」副词，不带用心的意象）

entries.definition: Wholly, with nothing excluded; often used with negatives.
entries.definitionCN: 完全地；全部地（常与否定词连用）

entries.definition: With attention to avoiding mistakes; it stresses caution rather than coverage.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细地；小心地（强调谨慎而非覆盖面）

entries.definition: Completely, almost always before a negative quality.
entries.definitionCN: 十足地；完全地（多修饰负面品质）

normalIntro.en: Real hooks from the word family: thorough, through, -ly, and the degree sense.
normalIntro.cn: 来自词族的真实钩子：thorough、through、后缀 -ly，以及程度用法。

normal.en: Thoroughly is thorough plus -ly, the ordinary way English turns an adjective into an adverb.
normal.cn: thoroughly 就是 thorough 加 -ly，英语把形容词变副词最常见的方式。

normal.en: A thorough search goes through everything, and thoroughly means doing it that way.
normal.cn: 彻底的搜查会把每样东西都翻 through，thoroughly 就是「以那种方式」。

normal.en: Thoroughly checked means no part was skipped.
normal.cn: 彻底检查过的意思是没有哪一部分被跳过。

normal.en: With feelings the word marks depth: thoroughly enjoy, thoroughly agree.
normal.cn: 与感受连用时它标记深度：十分享受、完全同意。

normal.en: With negative words it marks total failure: thoroughly wrong, thoroughly misguided.
normal.cn: 与负面词连用时它标记全盘失败：完全错误、彻底走偏。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp carried into every corner of a dark room until no shadow is left.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯被提进暗房的每个角落，直到不留一丝阴影。

abstract.en: Thoroughly is the sound of a job finished on the last step, not the middle one.
abstract.cn: thoroughly 是一件事在最后一步而非中途完成的声响。

abstract.en: Complete attention, complete feeling and complete failure all wear the same adverb.
abstract.cn: 完整的注意力、完整的感受、彻底的失败，戴的是同一个副词。

examples.en: She thoroughly enjoyed her first week at the new job.
examples.cn: 她在新工作的第一周过得十分愉快。

examples.en: The room was thoroughly cleaned before the guests arrived.
examples.cn: 客人到来前房间被彻底打扫过。

examples.en: I thoroughly disagree with that conclusion.
examples.cn: 我完全不同意那个结论。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑟若利」——瑟缩着把每寸地板都擦利落 → 彻底地

root: thoroughly = thorough（与 through 同源的日耳曼词根，意为「贯穿」，引申为「彻底」）+ 副词后缀 -ly；古英语同根词表示「直贯而过」，中古英语拼写分化后 thorough 专表「完全」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of thoroughly all measure completeness, applied to a task, a way of working, a feeling, or a bad judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: thoroughly 的四个义项都在衡量「完整」，分别用在任务、工作方式、感受与糟糕的判断上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp carried into every corner of a room until no shadow remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯被提进房间的每个角落，直到不留阴影。

branches.en: The task: every part covered, nothing skipped.
branches.cn: 任务线：每部分都覆盖，无一跳过。

branches.en: The worker: care that walks every step of the reading or check.
branches.cn: 做事者线：用心走完阅读或检查的每一步。

branches.en: The feeling: pleasure or agreement felt to the full.
branches.cn: 感受线：快乐或赞同被完整地感受到。

branches.en: The error: completeness measuring how deep the mistake goes.
branches.cn: 错误线：彻底衡量错误有多深。

branches.en: Coverage and care both come from the road image inside thorough.
branches.cn: 覆盖面与用心都来自 thorough 内部的道路意象。

intro.en: Thoroughly carries only native English endings: the adjective -ly pivot and the noun -ness.
intro.cn: thoroughly 只带英语本土词缀：构成副词的 -ly，以及构成名词的 -ness。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic with no Latin source, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词为日耳曼本土词，没有拉丁语来源，拉丁词条留空。

items.exampleCN: 它把 thorough 变成 thoroughly。

items.meaning: a public road through a place
items.example: The avenue is a busy thoroughfare.

items.meaning: from one side to the other
items.example: The train went through the tunnel.

items.exampleCN: 他们要求一场彻底的改革。

definition_zh: 虽然；尽管；可是；不过
definition_en: despite the fact that; used to introduce a contrast, or placed at the end of a clause to mean however
core_image: 话说到一半忽然拐个弯：前面点着头，后面却摇起头
scene: 朋友劝他别去山上，他笑着答应着，脚下还是往山路走。He set out for the summit though the clouds were closing in.
sceneCN: 这里 though 是「虽然、尽管」（第 1 个义项：让步从属连词）；句意为尽管乌云正在合拢，他还是出发去山顶了。

pos.zh: 虽然；尽管（引导让步状语从句）

collocations.zh: 与 though 用法相当的 although

derivatives.zh: 由 all 与 though 合成的连词，义为「虽然；尽管」
though 在网络与口语中的简写形式，义同「虽然」

senses.title: In spite of the fact that
senses.definition: used to introduce a fact that makes the main statement surprising or contrasting
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出一个使主句显得意外或形成对照的事实
senses.example: Though the road was steep, they reached the top before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 虽然山路陡峭，他们还是在中午前到达山顶。
senses.why: The word began as the same form as that, and grew into a marker that sets one clause against another.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初与 that 同形，后来演变成把一个分句与另一个分句对立起来的标记。

senses.title: However, at the end of a clause
senses.definition: placed at the end of a sentence to add a softer however or a second thought
senses.definitionCN: 放在句末，补充一个语气较软的「不过」或事后想法
senses.example: It is a small flat. Very cosy, though.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一套小公寓，不过很温馨。
senses.why: The contrast marker drifts to the end of the sentence, where it sounds like a spoken afterthought.
senses.whyCN: 这个转折标记漂到句末，听起来像说话人事后补上的念头。

senses.title: As if, in as though
senses.definition: in the phrase as though, meaning as if, used for an imagined situation
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 as though，意为「好像」，表示设想的情形
senses.example: He spoke as though he had known her for years.
senses.exampleCN: 他说话的样子好像已经认识她多年。
senses.why: Comparison and concession share one marker: a clause that does not quite match the main one.
senses.whyCN: 比较与让步共用一个标记：一个与主句并不完全相符的分句。

senses.title: Even though: a stronger concession
senses.definition: in the phrase even though, introducing a fact that does not change the result
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 even though，引出一个并不改变结果的事实
senses.example: Even though the shop was closed, a light still burned inside.
senses.exampleCN: 即使店铺已经关门，里面仍亮着灯。
senses.why: Adding even pushes the contrast to its limit: the fact is granted in full and the main clause still stands.
senses.whyCN: 加上 even 把对立推到极限：事实被完全承认，主句依然成立。

intro.en: Though is a native English word built on the old demonstrative stem, a close relative of that.
intro.cn: though 是英语本土词，建立在古老的指示词干之上，与 that 是近亲。

items.en: The Germanic demonstrative stem *þa- supplied words for pointing at something, including then and there.
items.cn: 日耳曼语指示词干 *þa- 提供了一批指称某物的词，包括 then 与 there。

items.en: Old English þeah was both a concessive conjunction and an adverb meaning nevertheless.
items.cn: 古英语 þeah 既是让步连词，也作副词表示「然而」。

items.en: Middle English spelling settled toward though, and the word kept both jobs, conjunction and sentence-final adverb.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写逐渐定为 though，这个词保留了两个用途：连词与句末副词。

items.en: The compound although, formed with all, became the more formal written choice, while though stayed common in speech.
items.cn: 由 all 构成的 although 成为更正式的书面选择，though 则在口语中保持常用。

items.en: As though and even though fixed the two special uses, comparison and reinforced concession.
items.cn: as though 与 even though 固定了两个专门用法：比拟与强化让步。

note.en: The first group separates the though family and its easily confused look-alikes; the second compares concessive and contrast words.
note.cn: 第一组区分 though 词族与易混的形近词；第二组比较让步与转折类词。

entries.definition: The formal written variant, all plus though, with the same concessive meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 虽然（all 与 though 复合，更书面）

entries.definition: From one side to the other; it differs by one letter and is often mistyped for though.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过；与 though 只差一个字母，常被误打

entries.definition: Complete and careful; another near spelling with a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底的；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: The past of think and a noun for an idea; it shares the th opening only.
entries.definitionCN: think 的过去式；只是开头字母相同，词源不同

entries.definition: An adverb of contrast that can start a sentence; stronger and more formal than final though.
entries.definitionCN: 然而（可置于句首，比句末 though 更正式）

entries.definition: In spite of that; a strongly formal contrast adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 然而；尽管如此（正式书面语）

entries.definition: Used to contrast two facts, especially in formal and legal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 而；然而（多用于正式与法律文本）

entries.definition: In spite of what has been said; a spoken contrast phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 即便如此（口语转折短语）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the real word family and the fixed phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自真实词族，以及这个词实际出现的固定短语。

normal.en: Although is all plus though, and it is the cooler, more written version.
normal.cn: although 就是 all 加 though，是更冷静、更书面的版本。

normal.en: As though is the same as as if: a scene that is only imagined.
normal.cn: as though 等于 as if：一个只是想象出来的场景。

normal.en: Even though grants the fact completely, then lets the main clause stand.
normal.cn: even though 先把事实完全承认，再让主句依然成立。

normal.en: Though at the end is a spoken afterthought, like a shrug after a sentence.
normal.cn: 句末的 though 是口语里的补充，像说完一句话后耸耸肩。

normal.en: Though is not through or thought: check the vowel and the ending before writing.
normal.cn: though 不是 through 也不是 thought：下笔前看清元音和结尾。

abstract.en: Picture a road sign that points forward and then bends: the main clause moves on, the concessive clause bends away.
abstract.cn: 想象一块指向前方又突然拐弯的路牌：主句继续前进，让步从句拐向一旁。

abstract.en: Though is the small hinge on which two opposite facts swing.
abstract.cn: though 是让两个相反事实摆动的那个小铰链。

abstract.en: The word nods at one fact and keeps walking toward the other.
abstract.cn: 这个词对一个事实点点头，然后继续走向另一个。

examples.en: Though she was tired, she finished the report that night.
examples.cn: 虽然很累，她当晚还是写完了报告。

examples.en: The soup was simple. It tasted good, though.
examples.cn: 汤很简单，不过味道不错。

examples.en: He looked as though he had seen a ghost.
examples.cn: 他看上去好像见了鬼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「豆」——嘴上说豆子好，转身把豆子推开 → though 虽然

root: 英语本土词，源自古英语 þeah，建立在日耳曼指示词干 *þa-（与 that、then 同源）之上；古英语中兼作让步连词与副词「然而」，后由 all + though 合成更书面的 although。

sensesIntro.en: All four uses of though mark a mismatch: a fact that does not stop the main clause, an afterthought at the end, an imagined comparison, and a concession pushed to its limit.
sensesIntro.cn: though 的四种用法都在标记「不相符」：挡不住主句的事实、句末的补充、设想中的比拟，以及推到极限的让步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence that nods at one fact and then turns its head to another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话先对一个事实点头，再扭头转向另一个事实。

branches.en: The standard concession: the fact is granted, the main clause still stands.
branches.cn: 标准让步线：事实被承认，主句依然成立。

branches.en: The spoken tail: contrast dropped at the end like an afterthought.
branches.cn: 口语尾音线：转折被丢到句末，像事后想起。

branches.en: The imagined scene: as though lines up a picture with reality.
branches.cn: 想象场景线：as though 把一幅画面与现实并列。

branches.en: The limit: even though grants everything and still holds.
branches.cn: 极限线：even though 全部承认之后依然成立。

branches.en: Written and spoken halves of the same hinge word.
branches.cn: 同一个铰链词的书面与口语两半。

intro.en: Though is a bare native word; its relatives come from compounds and spellings rather than suffixes.
intro.cn: though 是没有词缀的本土词，它的亲属来自复合与拼写变体，而非后缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is involved, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词不涉及拉丁语来源，拉丁词条留空。

items.meaning: in spite of the fact that
items.example: Although it rained, the game went on.
items.exampleCN: 虽然下雨，比赛照常进行。

items.example: She smiled as though nothing had happened.
items.exampleCN: 她笑着，好像什么都没发生。

items.example: Even though he tried, he failed.
items.exampleCN: 即使他努力了，还是失败了。

definition_zh: 体贴的；考虑周到的；沉思的；有思想的
definition_en: showing care for other people’s needs, or given to quiet and serious thinking
core_image: 一个人先在心里替你走一遍路，再把伞递到你手上
scene: 下雨的清晨，室友没说话，只在门口多放了一把伞和一张便条。It was thoughtful of her to leave an umbrella by the door on such a wet morning.
sceneCN: 这里 thoughtful 是「体贴的、考虑周到的」（第 1 个义项：替他人着想并付诸行动）；句意为她在这样的雨天把伞放在门口，真是体贴。

derivatives.zh: 由 think 不规则变化而来的名词，义为「想法；思考」，是 thoughtful 的词基
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「体贴地；沉思地」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「体贴；周到；深思」
由否定前缀 un- 加本词构成，义为「不体贴的；考虑不周的」

senses.title: Considerate of other people
senses.definition: showing that you think about other people’s feelings and needs and act to help
senses.definitionCN: 表现出替他人的感受与需要着想，并付诸行动
senses.example: It was thoughtful of him to call before dropping by.
senses.exampleCN: 他来访前先打了个电话，真是体贴。
senses.why: Thought plus the suffix -ful turns the inner act of thinking outward, into care for someone else.
senses.whyCN: thought 加上后缀 -ful，把内心的思考转向外部，变成对他人的照顾。

senses.title: Showing careful thought
senses.definition: carefully planned or considered, so that nothing important is forgotten
senses.definitionCN: 经过仔细计划或考虑，重要之处都没有遗漏
senses.example: The report offers a thoughtful analysis of the housing problem.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告对住房问题做了考虑周到的分析。
senses.why: The same fullness of thought is applied to a piece of work rather than to a person.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「思虑充盈」被用到一件作品上，而不是一个人身上。

senses.title: Quietly absorbed in thought
senses.definition: looking serious and quiet because you are thinking about something
senses.definitionCN: 因在思考某事而显得严肃、安静
senses.example: She sat by the window with a thoughtful expression.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐在窗边，一副若有所思的神情。
senses.why: This is the literal picture: a person whose face shows that the mind is full of thought.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的画面：脸上显出内心塞满思绪的人。

senses.title: Having serious ideas
senses.definition: showing serious and original ideas, of a person, book or film
senses.definitionCN: 指人、书或影片呈现出严肃而有独到见解的思想
senses.example: He is a thoughtful writer who asks uncomfortable questions.
senses.exampleCN: 他是一位有思想的作家，总提让人不适的问题。
senses.why: A mind that is always full of thought is valued for the quality of what it holds.
senses.whyCN: 总是装满意绪的心灵，因其所装之物的分量而受到重视。

intro.en: Thoughtful is a native English compound: the noun thought plus the full-suffix -ful.
intro.cn: thoughtful 是英语本土复合词：名词 thought 加表示「充满」的后缀 -ful。

items.en: The root behind think meant to seem or to appear to the mind, a sense still visible in an old legal phrase.
items.cn: think 背后的词根意为「在心中显现」，这一含义还残留在古老的固定说法里。

items.en: Old English had the verb for thinking and the noun for a thought, built on an old nominal form.
items.cn: 古英语已有表示「思考」的动词与表示「想法」的名词，建立在古老的名词形式上。

items.en: The adjective formed with -ful of thought appears in the Middle English period, first in the sense of being deep in thought.
items.cn: 由 thought 加 -ful 构成的形容词出现于中古英语时期，最初义为「陷入深思的」。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the word had moved outward: thoughtful came to mean considerate of other people.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，这个词向外转：thoughtful 开始表示「替他人着想的」。

items.en: Modern use keeps both directions side by side, the inner thinker and the outward kindness.
items.cn: 现代用法让两个方向并存：内心的思考者与向外的善意。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on thought; the second compares words of consideration and thinking.
note.cn: 第一组收以 thought 为词基的一族词；第二组比较表示体贴与思考的词。

entries.definition: The noun for an idea or the act of thinking, also the past of think.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「想法；思考」，也是 think 的过去式

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning in a considerate or meditative way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「体贴地；沉思地」

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being considerate or deep in thought.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「体贴、周到、深思」

entries.definition: Grateful; it rhymes with thoughtful and uses the same suffix but another base, so the root differs.
entries.definitionCN: 感激的；与本词押韵且后缀相同，但词基不同，词源不同

entries.definition: Careful not to trouble or hurt others; the closest formal partner of thoughtful.
entries.definitionCN: 体贴的；为他人着想的（最接近的正式近义词）

entries.definition: Paying close attention to someone and their needs.
entries.definitionCN: 殷勤的；关注他人需要的

entries.definition: Showing love and concern for others, warmer and more emotional.
entries.definitionCN: 关心人的（更温暖、更多情感色彩）

entries.definition: Quietly thinking, often with a hint of sadness.
entries.definitionCN: 沉思的（带一丝忧愁，文学色彩）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the base noun, the suffix -ful, and the outward turn the word took.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自词基名词、后缀 -ful，以及这个词后来向外的转向。

normal.en: Thoughtful is thought plus -ful: a head full of thought, aimed at someone else.
normal.cn: thoughtful 就是 thought 加 -ful：满脑子思绪，只是朝着别人的方向。

normal.en: A thoughtful gift shows that someone thought about you before choosing it.
normal.cn: 贴心的礼物说明有人先想到你，才去挑选。

normal.en: A thoughtful silence is a thinking silence, not an angry one.
normal.cn: thoughtful silence 是思考的静默，不是生气的静默。

normal.en: The adverb is thoughtfully, the noun thoughtfulness.
normal.cn: 副词是 thoughtfully，名词是 thoughtfulness。

normal.en: Do not mix it with thankful: one is care, the other is gratitude.
normal.cn: 不要与 thankful 相混：一个是体贴，一个是感激。

abstract.en: Picture someone walking your day in their head before it happens, then leaving what you will need.
abstract.cn: 想象有人在心里先把你的一天走一遍，然后把你需要的东西留下。

abstract.en: Thought is water; the suffix -ful makes it a cup filled to the brim, offered to someone.
abstract.cn: 思绪是水，后缀 -ful 让它成为满满一杯，端给别人。

abstract.en: The word points both inward to the quiet thinker and outward to the quiet helper.
abstract.cn: 这个词既指向内心的默想者，也指向安静的帮忙者。

examples.en: It was thoughtful of you to remember my birthday.
examples.cn: 你还记得我的生日，真是体贴。

examples.en: She gave the plan a thoughtful review before agreeing.
examples.cn: 她在同意前对这个计划做了周密的审视。

examples.en: He grew thoughtful whenever the name was mentioned.
examples.cn: 一提到那个名字，他就陷入沉思。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「梭特福」——心里来回穿梭,把福气先留给别人 → thoughtful 体贴的

root: 英语本土复合：thought（think 的不规则名词形，源自古英语表示「思考」的词）+ 后缀 -ful「充满……的」；最初指「陷入深思」，十八世纪起扩展为「替他人着想的」。

sensesIntro.en: Thoughtful fills the head with thought and then points it in two directions: outward to other people and their needs, inward to a quiet thinking mind.
sensesIntro.cn: thoughtful 让头脑装满思绪，再把这份思绪指向两个方向：向外给他人的需要，向内给安静的思考者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: walking someone else’s day inside your head, then leaving what they will need.
core.cn: 核心意象：在心里先替别人走一遍他的一天，再留下他会需要的东西。

branches.en: The person: thought turned into kindness for others.
branches.cn: 人线：思绪转化为对他人的善意。

branches.en: The work: the same fullness of thought spent on a report or a plan.
branches.cn: 作品线：同样的思虑充沛被用在报告或计划上。

branches.en: The face: the literal picture of a mind at work.
branches.cn: 面容线：心灵运转时最字面的画面。

branches.en: The writer: thoughts valuable enough to be a reputation.
branches.cn: 作者线：思绪深到足以成为一种名声。

branches.en: Inner and outer halves of the same suffixed word.
branches.cn: 同一个带后缀词的向内与向外两半。

intro.en: Thoughtful is built natively with the suffix -ful, and English adds -ly and -ness on top.
intro.cn: thoughtful 由本土后缀 -ful 构成，英语再在其上叠加 -ly 与 -ness。

latinIntro.en: The base and suffix are both English, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 词基与后缀都属英语，拉丁词条留空。

items.meaning: an idea; the act of thinking

items.example: We are thankful for your help.
A considerate host checks the heating.
items.exampleCN: 体贴的主人会查看暖气。

definition_zh: 一千；数以千计的；成千上万
definition_en: the number one thousand, or a very large number of people or things taken loosely
core_image: 一千枚小圆点排成整齐的方阵，一眼数不完
scene: 老街的夜市灯火通明,摊位前人头攒动,根本数不清。Thousands of people crowded into the old street for the night market.
sceneCN: 这里 thousand 是「数以千计的、成千上万的」（第 2 个义项：表示数量极多）；句意为成千上万的人涌进老街逛夜市。

collocations.zh: 数以千计的；成千上万的
千中之一；罕见的人或物

derivatives.zh: 由本词加序数后缀 -th 构成，义为「第一千；千分之一」
本词的复数形式，义为「数以千计；大量」
由本词加 -fold 构成，义为「千倍的；千倍地」

senses.title: The number one thousand
senses.definition: the number equal to ten times one hundred, written as 1000
senses.definitionCN: 等于一百的十倍、写作 1000 的数
senses.example: The hall can seat a thousand guests.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅能坐一千位客人。
senses.why: The word is a Germanic compound whose older meaning was a great hundred or a very large counted group.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是日耳曼语复合词，较早的意义是「大百」，即一个很大的计数单位。

senses.title: Very many, loosely counted
senses.definition: a very large but unspecified number, used in the plural with of
senses.definitionCN: 数量极大但不确切，复数后接 of
senses.example: Thousands of birds stop at the lake each autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 每年秋天都有成千上万只鸟在这片湖上停歇。
senses.why: Once the word meant a huge round count, it easily doubled as a word for too many to count.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既然表示一个很大的整数，就很容易兼表「多到数不过来」。

senses.title: One in a thousand: rare excellence
senses.definition: in the phrase one in a thousand, a person or thing that is unusually good
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 one in a thousand，指格外好的人或物
senses.example: A helper like her is one in a thousand.
senses.exampleCN: 像她这样的帮手是千中难求的。
senses.why: Thousand sets the price of rarity: pick one out of that whole crowd and it is special.
senses.whyCN: thousand 给稀有标了价：从那么一大群中挑出一个，它就是特别的。

senses.title: Used for emphasis in repetition
senses.definition: used in phrases such as a thousand times to stress how often something happens
senses.definitionCN: 用于 a thousand times 一类短语，强调某事发生的次数之多
senses.example: I have told you a thousand times to lock the door.
senses.exampleCN: 我跟你说过无数次要把门锁好。
senses.why: The number stands in for an unmeasured repetition, a spoken exaggeration rather than a real count.
senses.whyCN: 这个数字代替的是无法计量的重复，是口语夸张而非真实计数。

intro.en: Thousand is an old Germanic compound whose first part meant swelling or great and whose second part was the word for hundred.
intro.cn: thousand 是古老的日耳曼语复合词，前半表示「膨胀、巨大」，后半就是「百」这个词。

items.en: The compound combined a root for swelling or being great with the word hundred, giving a great hundred, the biggest old unit.
items.cn: 这个复合词把表示「膨胀、巨大」的词根与 hundred 组合，构成「大百」，是古代最大的计数单位。

items.en: Old English ðusend kept both halves recognisable and still carried the sense of a vast round number.
items.cn: 古英语 ðusend 仍能辨认出两半，并保留「庞大的整数」的含义。

items.en: Norse settlers used a closely related form, which helped fix the modern th- sound and spelling.
items.cn: 北欧移民使用与之密切相关的形式，帮助固定了现代以 th- 开头的读音与拼写。

items.en: Middle English thousand settled as a plain numeral once the decimal system of counting spread.
items.cn: 十进制计数铺开之后，中古英语 thousand 固定为单纯的数词。

items.en: Modern English uses the plural thousands for loose bigness and keeps a thousand times as an exaggeration.
items.cn: 现代英语用复数 thousands 表示含糊的「极多」，并保留 a thousand times 这类夸张说法。

note.en: The first group lines up the counting words around thousand; the second compares words for very large numbers.
note.cn: 第一组排开 thousand 周边的计数词；第二组比较表示极大数量的词。

entries.definition: The ordinal, meaning the one in position one thousand.
entries.definitionCN: 序数词，义为「第一千」

entries.definition: The plural used for an unspecified large number.
entries.definitionCN: 复数，义为「数以千计」

entries.definition: The unit inside the old compound; a hundred on its own.
entries.definitionCN: 百；是古老的复合词后半，单独表示一百

entries.definition: A thousand times as much, formed with -fold.
entries.definitionCN: 千倍的；由 -fold 构成

entries.definition: One thousand thousands; a far larger round number.
entries.definitionCN: 百万；比千大得多的整数

entries.definition: A countless number, used formally or in literature.
entries.definitionCN: 无数（书面、文学色彩）

entries.definition: Too many to be counted; it gives no exact figure at all.
entries.definitionCN: 数不清的（完全不给出数目）

entries.definition: A large enough amount; it stresses enough rather than number.
entries.definitionCN: 大量（强调充足而非计数）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the two halves of the compound and from the plural pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自这个复合词的两半，以及复数的用法规律。

normal.en: The second half is the word hundred: thousand began as a great hundred.
normal.cn: 后半就是 hundred 这个词：thousand 起初指「大百」。

normal.en: Thousands of keeps the plural -s and the preposition of.
normal.cn: thousands of 保留复数 -s 并跟介词 of。

normal.en: A thousand is exact when you count money, but loose in a thousand times.
normal.cn: 数钱时 a thousand 是精确的，在 a thousand times 里却是含糊的。

normal.en: The ordinal is thousandth, with -th, like fourth and fifth.
normal.cn: 序数词是 thousandth，加 -th，与 fourth、fifth 同类。

normal.en: One in a thousand means rare, not exactly the thousandth one.
normal.cn: one in a thousand 意为罕见，并不是恰好第一千个。

abstract.en: Picture a grid of little dots ten by ten by ten, a cube you cannot count at a glance.
abstract.cn: 想象十乘十乘十的小圆点方阵，一个一眼数不完的立方体。

abstract.en: The word is a big round stone: say it and the group it names becomes one thing.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一块圆圆的大石头：一说出口，它所命名的群体就变成一个整体。

abstract.en: Thousand is where counting stops being careful and starts being a feeling for size.
abstract.cn: thousand 是计数从认真转向「规模感」的地方。

examples.en: The old stadium holds about twenty thousand people.
examples.cn: 这座老体育场能容纳约两万人。

examples.en: Thousands of letters arrived after the programme was shown.
examples.cn: 节目播出后，成千上万封信寄来了。

examples.en: A friend like that is one in a thousand.
examples.cn: 那样的朋友是千中难求的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扫灶的」——一千个人排队扫灶，队伍长得望不到头 → thousand 一千

root: 日耳曼语复合词：前半词根表示「膨胀、巨大」，后半即 hundred「百」，合起来是古代最大的计数单位「大百」；古英语作 ðusend，古北欧语近缘形式固定了 th- 音，后随十进制普及成为单纯数词「一千」。

sensesIntro.en: Thousand moves from an exact round count to a loose bigness, then to a measure of rarity and of endless repetition.
sensesIntro.cn: thousand 从一个精确的大整数，扩展为含糊的「极多」，再引申出「稀有」与「无尽重复」两种用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cube of little dots, ten by ten by ten, too many to count in one glance.
core.cn: 核心意象：十乘十乘十的小圆点立方体，一眼数不完。

branches.en: The exact count: ten hundreds, written as a number.
branches.cn: 精确计数线：十个一百，写作一个数字。

branches.en: The loose crowd: thousands of, too many to bother counting.
branches.cn: 含糊人群线：thousands of，多到懒得去数。

branches.en: The rare one: chosen out of the whole crowd.
branches.cn: 稀有线：从整群中挑出的那一个。

branches.en: The exaggeration: a number standing in for endless repetition.
branches.cn: 夸张线：用一个数字代替无尽的重复。

branches.en: Precision and vagueness both live in the same round word.
branches.cn: 精确与含糊都住在同一个圆整的词里。

intro.en: Thousand takes the ordinal -th and the multiplier -fold; the plural -s does the rest.
intro.cn: thousand 可加序数后缀 -th 与倍数后缀 -fold，其余由复数 -s 承担。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, with no Latin source, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词为日耳曼语来源，没有拉丁语成分，拉丁词条留空。

items.structure: second half of the old compound

definition_zh: 第一千；千分之一
definition_en: coming after the nine hundred and ninety-ninth in order, or one of a thousand equal parts
core_image: 一条刻满小格的长尺，第一千格恰好是最后一格
scene: 计时器屏幕上数字飞速滚动,终于停在一个极小的刻度上。His final run was decided by a thousandth of a second.
sceneCN: 这里 thousandth 是「千分之一」（第 2 个义项：一千等分之一）；句意为他的最后一跑以千分之一秒之差决出胜负。

forms.label: 小数读法中的分数用法

derivatives.zh: 去掉序数后缀 -th 得到的基数词，义为「一千」
由基数词加 -fold 构成，义为「千倍的」
基数词的复数，义为「数以千计」

senses.title: The one in position one thousand
senses.definition: coming after the nine hundred and ninety-ninth in a series or order
senses.definitionCN: 在序列中排在第九百九十九之后
senses.example: The thousandth visitor to the museum received a small gift.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的第一千位访客收到了一份小礼物。
senses.why: The ordinal -th simply marks a position in the long counting line.
senses.whyCN: 序数后缀 -th 只是标出这条长长计数线上的一个位置。

senses.title: One of a thousand equal parts
senses.definition: one of a thousand equal divisions of a whole, especially of a unit of measurement
senses.definitionCN: 把一个整体等分成一千份中的一份，尤用于计量单位
senses.example: The lens is polished to within a thousandth of a millimetre.
senses.exampleCN: 这块镜片被磨到误差不超过千分之一毫米。
senses.why: Once the word names the thousandth place, it doubles as a very small fraction.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦命名第一千格，也就兼任极小分数的角色。

senses.title: For the last time in a long count
senses.definition: in phrases such as the thousandth time, used to mean far too many times
senses.definitionCN: 用于 the thousandth time 等短语，表示次数多到不胜其烦
senses.example: For the thousandth time, please close the window.
senses.exampleCN: 我都说过一千次了，请把窗户关上。
senses.why: The exact ordinal turns into a speaker’s exasperation, an exaggeration for endless repetition.
senses.whyCN: 精确的序数词变成说话人的恼火，是对无尽重复的夸张说法。

intro.en: Thousandth is thousand plus the ordinary English ordinal ending -th, exactly as fourth and fifth are made.
intro.cn: thousandth 就是 thousand 加英语常见的序数后缀 -th，与 fourth、fifth 构词方式完全相同。

items.en: The base is the old compound meaning a great hundred, discussed under thousand.
items.cn: 词基就是表示「大百」的古老复合词，详见 thousand 条目。

items.en: Old English already had the ordinal of the large counting word, marking a position in a long series.
items.cn: 古英语已有这个大写计数词的序数形式，用来标记长序列中的一个位置。

items.en: Middle English dropped the old irregular ordinal endings and extended -th to most numerals.
items.cn: 中古英语淘汰了古老的不规则序数词尾，把 -th 推广到绝大多数数词。

items.en: By early modern English the spelling thousandth was fixed, both for order and for the fraction.
items.cn: 到早期现代英语，thousandth 的拼写已经固定，既表顺序也表分数。

items.en: Science popularised the fractional use, since a thousandth of a unit is a useful very small measure.
items.cn: 科学计量推广了它的分数用法，因为一个单位的千分之一是很有用的极小量。

note.en: The first group lines up ordinal neighbours; the second compares small fractions and large counts.
note.cn: 第一组排开相邻的序数词；第二组比较小分数与大数量。

entries.definition: The ordinal of hundred, with the same -th ending.
entries.definitionCN: 百的序数词，加同样的 -th

entries.definition: The ordinal of million, one step further up the scale.
entries.definitionCN: 百万的序数词，在刻度上再进一档

entries.definition: The ordinal of ten; -th after a vowel sound behaves differently.
entries.definitionCN: 十的序数词；接元音后时 -th 的读音不同

entries.definition: The cardinal form, one thousand.
entries.definitionCN: 基数词，义为「一千」

entries.definition: A part of a whole number; the general word that thousandth is one kind of.
entries.definitionCN: 分数；千分之一属于其中的一类

entries.definition: A number written with a point, such as nought point nought nought one for a thousandth.
entries.definitionCN: 小数；千分之一写作小数点后三位

entries.definition: Extremely small; a description of size with no measure attached.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的（只描述大小，不带刻度）

entries.definition: One of two equal parts; the most familiar fraction for contrast.
entries.definitionCN: 一半（最常见的分数，用于对照）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the -th pattern and the fractional use in measurement.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自 -th 序数规律，以及在计量中的分数用法。

normal.en: Add -th to thousand, just as fourth and fifth carry their -th.
normal.cn: 在 thousand 后加 -th，正如 fourth 与 fifth 都带着 -th。

normal.en: A thousandth of a second is the number on the sports timer’s last screen.
normal.cn: 千分之一秒就是计时器最后那一屏上的数字。

normal.en: The ordinal marks place, the fraction marks a slice: one word, two jobs.
normal.cn: 序数标记位置，分数标记切片：一个词，两种职责。

normal.en: The thousandth visitor is a milestone; a thousandth of a second is a hair’s breadth.
normal.cn: 第一千位访客是一个里程碑；千分之一秒却细如发丝。

normal.en: For the thousandth time is not a count but a complaint.
normal.cn: for the thousandth time 不是计数，而是抱怨。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler carved into a thousand tiny squares, with the last square lit up.
abstract.cn: 想象一把被刻成一千个小格的尺子，最后一格亮着。

abstract.en: The same word can be the summit of a count or an almost invisible sliver.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既可以是计数的顶点，也可以是一片几乎看不见的细条。

abstract.en: Thousandth is where large numbers teach you how small small can be.
abstract.cn: thousandth 是「大数量」教你「小」能小到什么程度的地方。

examples.en: The race was decided by three thousandths of a second.
examples.cn: 这场比赛以千分之三秒之差分出胜负。

examples.en: This was the thousandth copy printed from the old press.
examples.cn: 这是那台老印刷机印出的第一千份。

examples.en: For the thousandth time, put the tools back in the box.
examples.cn: 我都说了一千遍了，把工具放回箱子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扫芯斯」——扫到第一千根芯丝,只剩那么一丝 → thousandth 千分之一

root: thousand（日耳曼语复合词，原指「大百、千」）+ 序数后缀 -th，与 fourth、fifth 构词相同；既表序列中的第一千个，也表一千等分之一，后者在现代计量中尤为常用。

sensesIntro.en: Thousandth has one exact position, one tiny fraction, and one exasperated exaggeration to cover.
sensesIntro.cn: thousandth 要覆盖一个精确位置、一个极小分数，以及一个烦躁的夸张说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler cut into a thousand small squares, with the last one lit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把被刻成一千小格的尺子，最后一格亮着。

branches.en: The position: the last step of the first thousand.
branches.cn: 位置线：第一个千的最后一步。

branches.en: The slice: one of a thousand equal parts.
branches.cn: 切片线：一千等份中的一份。

branches.en: The complaint: a count worn out by repetition.
branches.cn: 抱怨线：被重复磨掉分量的计数。

branches.en: Precision work, where a thousandth of a unit is a real difference.
branches.cn: 精密工作线：单位的千分之一是真实的差别。

branches.en: Exact order and exhausted exaggeration share the same form.
branches.cn: 精确的顺序与疲惫的夸张共用同一形式。

intro.en: Thousandth is a clean -th ordinal; related forms come from the base numeral.
intro.cn: thousandth 是标准的 -th 序数词，相关形式都从基数词派生。

latinIntro.en: Both the base and the suffix are native English, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 词基与后缀都属英语本土，拉丁词条留空。

items.exampleCN: 它把 thousand 变成 thousandth。

definition_zh: 线；细丝；线索；思路；螺纹；（网络）帖子
definition_en: a very thin strand of cotton or other fibre, or a connecting line of thought, story or discussion
core_image: 一根极细的线穿过针眼，把散开的布片一点点连起来
scene: 老人补旧棉袄,眯着眼把一根细白的线往针眼里送了三次才穿过去。She licked the end of the thread and pushed it through the eye of the needle.
sceneCN: 这里 thread 是「线、细丝」（第 1 个义项：缝纫用的极细纤维）；句意为她舔湿线头，把它穿进针眼。

derivatives.zh: thread 与 bare 复合，义为「（布料）磨得起毛露线的；陈腐的」
由本词加 -like 构成，义为「线状的；细如丝的」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「穿线；螺纹加工」

senses.title: A thin strand for sewing
senses.definition: a very thin strand of cotton, silk or other fibre, used to sew cloth or weave fabric
senses.definitionCN: 棉、丝或其他纤维制成的极细股线，用于缝布或织布
senses.example: She pulled a red thread through the hem of the curtain.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一根红线穿过了窗帘的下摆。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a twisted fibre, spun thin enough to pass through a needle’s eye.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意义是搓成的纤维，细到能穿过针眼。

senses.title: A connecting line of thought
senses.definition: the connecting line that holds an argument, story or explanation together
senses.definitionCN: 把论证、故事或解释串起来的连接线索
senses.example: I lost the thread of his argument halfway through.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲到一半，我就跟不上他的论证思路了。
senses.why: A thread runs invisibly through cloth; an argument has just such a line running through it.
senses.whyCN: 线在布中看不见地延伸；一段论证里也正有这样一条线。

senses.title: A thin line of something
senses.definition: a thin stream or line of liquid, smoke, light or similar
senses.definitionCN: 液体、烟、光等形成的一缕细流
senses.example: A thin thread of smoke rose from the chimney.
senses.exampleCN: 一缕细细的烟从烟囱里升起。
senses.why: Anything stretched thin enough to look like a strand borrows the word.
senses.whyCN: 凡是拉得足够细、看起来像股线的东西，都可以借用这个词。

senses.title: A ridge on a screw
senses.definition: the continuous spiral ridge cut around a screw, bolt or pipe
senses.definitionCN: 螺钉、螺栓或管子上连续盘旋的凸棱
senses.example: The thread on this bolt is worn and no longer grips.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗螺栓的螺纹磨损了，已经拧不住。
senses.why: A spiral ridge is literally a thread wound round a cylinder, the image carried into metal.
senses.whyCN: 螺旋凸棱本就是把线绕在圆柱上，这个意象被带进了金属里。

senses.title: A linked online discussion
senses.definition: a series of linked messages on a forum or social platform, replies hanging under one post
senses.definitionCN: 论坛或社交平台上一串相互关联的留言，回复挂在一个帖子下
senses.example: Her question drew a long thread of replies.
senses.exampleCN: 她的问题引来了一长串回复。
senses.why: The digital thread is stitched from messages: each reply is sewn onto the one before.
senses.whyCN: 网络上的串由一条条消息缝成：每个回复都被缝在前一条上。

senses.title: To pass through a narrow space
senses.definition: to move carefully through a narrow space or a crowd, or to pass something through a small opening
senses.definitionCN: 小心地穿过狭窄空间或人群，或把某物穿过小孔
senses.example: We threaded our way through the market crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在市场的人流中穿行而过。
senses.why: The verb keeps the needle image: something thin is pushed through a small gap.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了针的意象：细长之物被推过狭小的缝隙。

intro.en: Thread is a native English word whose root meant to twist; the same root lies behind throw and through.
intro.cn: thread 是英语本土词，词根意为「搓、扭」；同一个词根也藏在 throw 与 through 里。

items.en: The root meant to twist or wind, which describes exactly how fibre is spun into thread.
items.cn: 词根意为「搓、缠」，正是纤维被纺成线的过程。

items.en: Old English þræd meant a fine spun cord, and the verb form already meant to pass through a narrow opening.
items.cn: 古英语 þræd 意为细纺成的线，其动词形式已表示「穿过狭窄处」。

items.en: Middle English used the noun for both sewing fibre and the warp of cloth, and began the figurative sense of a line of speech.
items.cn: 中古英语用这个名词兼指缝线与本布的经线，并开始出现「话里的线」这类比喻。

items.en: By the nineteenth century a thread could be any thin line, from smoke to a mountain path.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，thread 可以指任何细线，从一缕烟到一条山径。

items.en: The digital age added one more: an online thread where replies hang from one message.
items.cn: 数字时代又添一义：回复挂在一条消息下的网络帖子。

note.en: The first group gathers the twisted-root family and near spellings; the second compares thin lines and linked sequences.
note.cn: 第一组收「搓、扭」词根的一族词与形近词；第二组比较细线与相互关联的序列。

entries.definition: Worn so thin that the threads show; also used of tired, stale ideas.
entries.definitionCN: 磨得露线的；也指陈旧乏味的

entries.definition: Thin and long like a thread.
entries.definitionCN: 细长如线的

entries.definition: A warning of harm; a near spelling with a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 威胁；与 thread 拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: To send something through the air; it shares the twisted, turning root.
entries.definitionCN: 投掷；与 thread 同属「扭、转」词根

entries.definition: A thicker cord, or a series of items on one line.
entries.definitionCN: 细绳；一串（比 thread 粗，且常用于成串之物）

entries.definition: Spun fibre used for knitting, thicker than sewing thread.
entries.definitionCN: 纱；毛线（比缝线粗，用于编织）

entries.definition: A single thin length of hair, rope or fibre.
entries.definitionCN: 一缕；一股（单根细长之物）

entries.definition: A piece of evidence that guides an investigation; it shares the image of a guiding thread.
entries.definitionCN: 线索（与「引路之线」意象相通）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the twisting root, the needle image, and the later figurative senses.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自「搓、扭」词根、针线意象，以及后起的比喻义。

normal.en: The root meant to twist, and thread is fibre twisted into a single fine line.
normal.cn: 词根意为「搓」，thread 就是被搓成一根细线的纤维。

normal.en: Thread a needle keeps the physical picture, and threading through a crowd keeps the same narrow gap.
normal.cn: thread a needle 保留实物画面，threading through a crowd 保留同一个窄缝。

normal.en: Lose the thread means the line of an argument has slipped out of your hand.
normal.cn: lose the thread 意为论证的那根线从手中滑走了。

normal.en: A thread of hope is the thinnest possible line of it.
normal.cn: a thread of hope 是希望细到不能再细的一线。

normal.en: An online thread is messages sewn one after another.
normal.cn: 网络 thread 是一条条消息被缝在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a single white thread crossing a dark cloth: the cloth is the topic, the thread is the point.
abstract.cn: 想象一根白线穿过深色布料：布是话题，线才是要点。

abstract.en: Anything long and thin, from smoke to a path, is the same line drawn with another material.
abstract.cn: 凡细长之物，从烟到小径，都是用另一种材料画出的同一条线。

abstract.en: Pull one thread and the whole cloth moves: that is how an idea holds a story together.
abstract.cn: 抽动一根线，整块布都动：这就是一个念头如何撑起一个故事。

examples.en: Use a darker thread so the stitches will not show.
examples.cn: 用深一点的线，这样针脚就不显眼。

examples.en: Try to follow the thread of the story to the end.
examples.cn: 试着顺着故事的线索读到结尾。

examples.en: We threaded through the narrow lanes of the old town.
examples.cn: 我们穿行在老城的窄巷中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「思锐的」——思绪锐利得像一根细线，穿过所有乱麻 → thread 线；思路

root: 古英语 þræd，源自日耳曼词根「搓、扭」，本指纺成的细线；同根词还有 throw「投掷」与 through「穿过」。由实物之线引申出思路、细流、螺纹与网络帖子等义。

sensesIntro.en: Thread begins as twisted fibre and then lends its thin connecting line to thought, smoke, screws, crowds and online replies.
sensesIntro.cn: thread 从搓成的纤维开始，再把这根细连接线借给思路、烟缕、螺纹、人群与网络回复。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one white thread crossing a dark cloth and holding the pieces together.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根白线穿过深色布料，把布片连在一起。

branches.en: The object: fibre thin enough for a needle.
branches.cn: 实物线：细到能穿针的纤维。

branches.en: The invisible line: through an argument or through the air as smoke.
branches.cn: 无形线：穿过论证，或以烟的形式穿过空气。

branches.en: The metal line: a ridge wound like thread round a bolt.
branches.cn: 金属线：像线一样绕在螺栓上的凸棱。

branches.en: The shared line: replies stitched to one message online.
branches.cn: 共享线：网络上缝在同一条消息上的回复。

branches.en: The action: pushing something thin through a narrow gap.
branches.cn: 动作线：把细长之物推过窄缝。

intro.en: Thread compounds freely with bare and like, and the verb takes ordinary -ing and -ed endings.
intro.cn: thread 能与 bare、like 自由复合，动词则加普通的 -ing 与 -ed。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词为日耳曼本土词，拉丁词条留空。

items.meaning: from one side to the other

definition_zh: 威胁；恐吓；危险；凶兆
definition_en: a statement or sign that someone intends to harm you, or a person or thing likely to cause danger
core_image: 有人把拳头举在半空，还没落下，空气先紧了一层
scene: 山脚的村子连下了半个月的雨,老人盯着裂开的山脊不肯睡。The cracked hillside was a threat to every house in the valley.
sceneCN: 这里 threat 是「威胁、危险的事物」（第 3 个义项：可能造成危害的人或事物）；句意为裂开的山坡对山谷里每座房子都是威胁。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加动词后缀 -en 构成，义为「威胁；恐吓；危及」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「威胁的；凶险的」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「受到威胁的；濒危的」

senses.title: A stated intention to harm
senses.definition: a warning, spoken or written, that someone will hurt or punish you if you do not do something
senses.definitionCN: 口头或书面警告，若不照做就会受到伤害或惩罚
senses.example: He made a threat that he would report the missing money.
senses.exampleCN: 他威胁说要举报那笔失踪的钱。
senses.why: The root means to press or squeeze: a threat is pressure applied before any blow falls.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「压、挤」：威胁是在拳头落下之前施加的压力。

senses.title: The feeling of danger
senses.definition: a sense that harm is close, whether or not words have been spoken
senses.definitionCN: 感到伤害临近，无论是否有人说过什么
senses.example: The quiet in the room carried a threat that none of them could name.
senses.exampleCN: 屋里那片安静带着一种谁也说不清的威胁。
senses.why: The noun can name a felt pressure even when nobody has spoken a word.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有人开口，这个名词也能命名一种被感觉到的压迫。

senses.title: A person or thing that endangers
senses.definition: a person, group or thing likely to cause harm or trouble
senses.definitionCN: 可能造成伤害或麻烦的人、群体或事物
senses.example: Rising sea levels are a threat to low-lying islands.
senses.exampleCN: 海平面上升对低洼岛屿是一种威胁。
senses.why: Pressure can come from a storm as easily as from a person, so the word names the source too.
senses.whyCN: 压力可以来自一场风暴，也可以来自一个人，于是这个词也用来命名那个源头。

senses.title: A sign of coming harm
senses.definition: an early sign that something bad is likely to happen
senses.definitionCN: 某事可能发生坏结果的早期迹象
senses.example: Those dark clouds were a threat of hail.
senses.exampleCN: 那些乌云是冰雹的凶兆。
senses.why: A threat can be read in the sky before it is ever spoken: the sign itself carries the pressure.
senses.whyCN: 威胁可以在开口之前就读到天上：兆头本身就带着那股压力。

intro.en: Threat is a native English word from a Germanic root meaning to press or squeeze, the same pressure image behind throng.
intro.cn: threat 是英语本土词，源自意为「压、挤」的日耳曼词根，throng「拥挤」背后是同样的压迫意象。

items.en: The root carried the idea of pressing, crowding or forcing, a physical pressure on someone.
items.cn: 这个词根带有「压、挤、逼迫」之意，是对某人施加的实体压迫。

items.en: Old English þreat meant a crowd or a troop as well as pressure and compulsion, an army being pressure in human form.
items.cn: 古英语 þreat 既指人群、队伍，也指压迫与强制，一支军队就是人形的压力。

items.en: Middle English narrowed the word to the danger a hostile force represents, whether words or warriors.
items.cn: 中古英语把词义收窄为敌对力量所代表的危险，无论那是言语还是兵马。

items.en: The verb threat was replaced by threaten, built with the -en ending, and the noun kept the plain form.
items.cn: 动词形式 threat 被以 -en 结尾的 threaten 取代，名词则保留原形。

items.en: Modern English extends the noun to impersonal dangers, so a virus or a rising sea can be a threat.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个名词扩展到非人的危险，病毒或上涨的海面都能成为威胁。

note.en: The first group gathers the threat family and near spellings; the second compares words for warnings and danger.
note.cn: 第一组收 threat 词族与形近词；第二组比较表示警告与危险的词。

entries.definition: The verb, to say or show that you will harm someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「威胁、恐吓」

entries.definition: The adjective for behaviour or weather that menaces.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「威胁的、凶险的」

entries.definition: A thin line of fibre; one letter apart but from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 线；与 threat 只差一个字母，词源不同

entries.definition: To behave towards someone or give medical care; the spelling is close, the root is not.
entries.definitionCN: 对待；治疗（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: A statement that something bad may happen; it informs rather than pressures.
entries.definitionCN: 警告（重在告知，而非施压）

entries.definition: A serious threat or a threatening person; stronger in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 威胁；危险人物（语气更强）

entries.definition: The general possibility of harm, without anyone intending it.
entries.definitionCN: 危险（泛指伤害的可能，无人有意）

entries.definition: The act of frightening someone into doing what you want, often by law.
entries.definitionCN: 恐吓（常指以恐吓迫使服从，法律用词）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the pressing root, the verb family, and the wide modern use.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自「压」的词根、动词词族，以及现代扩展的用法。

normal.en: The root means to press, and a threat is pressure put on before anything is done.
normal.cn: 词根意为「压」，威胁是在事情发生前施加的压力。

normal.en: Threaten is the verb, built with -en, and the noun stays short.
normal.cn: threaten 是加 -en 构成的动词，名词则保持短小。

normal.en: An empty threat has no army behind it, only words.
normal.cn: empty threat 背后没有兵马，只有言语。

normal.en: Under threat means the pressure has already arrived.
normal.cn: under threat 意为压力已经临头。

normal.en: A storm, a virus or a rising sea can pose a threat, with no person involved.
normal.cn: 风暴、病毒或上涨的海面都能构威胁，其中没有人的身影。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand that never comes down: the waiting is the threat.
abstract.cn: 想象一只举起却始终没落下的手：等待本身就是威胁。

abstract.en: A threat is danger that has learned to speak.
abstract.cn: 威胁是学会了说话的危险。

abstract.en: Threat is the shadow cast forward by something bad still on its way.
abstract.cn: 威胁是尚未到达的坏事提前投下的影子。

examples.en: The letter contained a threat to burn the warehouse.
examples.cn: 这封信里威胁要烧掉仓库。

examples.en: Pollution is the greatest threat to the river.
examples.cn: 污染是这条河最大的威胁。

examples.en: Nobody took his threat seriously.
examples.cn: 没人把他的威胁当真。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死拽的」——被人死拽着衣领不让走，那种逼迫感 → threat 威胁

root: 古英语 þreat，源自日耳曼词根「压、挤、逼迫」，本兼指人群、队伍与压迫；中古英语收窄为敌对力量的危险，动词后由 threaten 承担。

sensesIntro.en: Threat keeps one image of pressure and moves it from spoken words to a feeling, a dangerous source and a sign in the sky.
sensesIntro.cn: threat 保持「压迫」这一个意象，从说出的话挪到一个感觉、一个危险源，以及天上的兆头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised hand that never falls, holding the air tight.
core.cn: 核心意象：举起却始终不落的手，让空气绷紧。

branches.en: The words: someone names the harm they will do.
branches.cn: 言语线：有人说出他将要施加的伤害。

branches.en: The feeling: pressure sensed before anything is said.
branches.cn: 感觉线：什么都没说，压力先被感到。

branches.en: The source: a virus, a sea or a person that endangers.
branches.cn: 源头线：病毒、海水或某个人构成危险。

branches.en: The sign: clouds or cracks that foretell harm.
branches.cn: 兆头线：预示伤害的乌云或裂缝。

branches.en: Said and unsaid pressure are the same word.
branches.cn: 说出的压力与未说出的压力是同一个词。

intro.en: Threat stays bare as a noun; the family grows through -en and -ing.
intro.cn: threat 作名词保持原形；词族通过 -en 与 -ing 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic with no Latin source, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词为日耳曼本土词，没有拉丁语来源，拉丁词条留空。

items.example: He was a menace on the road.

definition_zh: 威胁；恐吓；危及；预示凶险
definition_en: to say that you will harm someone, to put someone or something in danger, or to seem about to do something bad
core_image: 天边推过来一整片乌云，压得人抬不起头
scene: 堤坝上的水位一夜涨了三尺,守夜人不停往村里打电话。The rising flood threatened the whole village.
sceneCN: 这里 threaten 是「危及、威胁到」（第 2 个义项：使某事处于危险中）；句意为上涨的洪水危及整个村庄。

collocations.zh: 威胁要做某事；眼看就要……

derivatives.zh: 由动词去掉后缀 -en 得到的名词，义为「威胁；危险」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「威胁的；凶险的」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「受到威胁的；濒危的」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「威胁地」

senses.title: To say you will harm someone
senses.definition: to tell someone that you will hurt them or cause trouble unless they do what you want
senses.definitionCN: 告诉对方若不听命就会伤害他或制造麻烦
senses.example: The caller threatened to publish the photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 打电话的人威胁说要公布那些照片。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an act: pressure is applied out loud, before any blow.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：压力在拳头落下之前就大喊着施加出来。

senses.title: To put in danger
senses.definition: to be likely to harm someone or something, of a thing rather than a person
senses.definitionCN: 指事物而非人可能造成伤害
senses.example: Smoke from the factory threatens the health of nearby residents.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂排出的烟危及附近居民的健康。
senses.why: Pressure need not come from a voice; a flood or a policy presses in just as hard.
senses.whyCN: 压力不必来自声音；洪水或政策压得同样沉。

senses.title: To seem about to happen
senses.definition: to look as if something bad is going to happen, of clouds, events or a situation
senses.definitionCN: 指乌云、事件或局势看起来即将发生坏事
senses.example: Dark clouds threatened rain all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 整个下午乌云都预示着一场雨。
senses.why: The verb lets an inanimate thing lean forward: the sky itself seems to be pressing.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词让无生命之物也前倾身体：连天空看起来都在施压。

senses.title: To endanger an institution or system
senses.definition: to put the continued existence of an organisation, system or custom at risk
senses.definitionCN: 使组织、制度或习俗的存续面临风险
senses.example: The cuts threaten the future of the local library.
senses.exampleCN: 这些削减让本地图书馆的未来岌岌可危。
senses.why: Once anything can press, the passive follows easily: a library, a language or a job can be threatened.
senses.whyCN: 一旦任何事物都能施压，被动式便顺理成章：图书馆、语言或工作都能处于威胁之下。

intro.en: Threaten is the verb made from the noun threat with the Germanic suffix -en, which also makes widen and strengthen.
intro.cn: threaten 是由名词 threat 加日耳曼语后缀 -en 构成的动词，widen、strengthen 也是同样的做法。

items.en: The old root meant to press or crowd, the pressure behind both threat and throng.
items.cn: 古老词根意为「压、挤」，威胁与 throng 背后的压迫感同源。

items.en: Old English had a verb of the same shape meaning to press or force, alongside the noun for a crowd and for compulsion.
items.cn: 古英语已有同形动词表示「压迫、胁迫」，与表示人群和强制的名词并存。

items.en: Middle English rebuilt the verb on the noun with -en, and threaten came to mean uttering harm or showing danger.
items.cn: 中古英语以名词为词基加 -en 重造动词，threaten 遂表示「扬言伤害」或「显露危险」。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the verb extended to things: clouds, storms and diseases could threaten.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，这个动词扩展到事物：乌云、风暴与疾病都能 threaten。

items.en: Modern English uses the passive freely, so a species can be threatened with extinction.
items.cn: 现代英语大量使用被动式，于是可以说某个物种面临灭绝的威胁。

note.en: The first group gathers the threat family; the second compares verbs of menacing and warning.
note.cn: 第一组收 threat 词族；第二组比较表示威胁与警告的动词。

entries.definition: The noun, a warning of harm or a source of danger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「威胁；危险」

entries.definition: The adjective for a menacing look, letter or sky.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「威胁的、凶险的」

entries.definition: The adjective for something put at risk, as in an endangered species.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「受到威胁的、濒危的」

entries.definition: To make strong, built with the same -en ending but another base, so the root differs.
entries.definitionCN: 加强；与本词同为 -en 动词，但词基不同，词源不同

entries.definition: To be a threat to someone, often of a person or mood.
entries.definitionCN: 威胁；对……构成危险（正式）

entries.definition: To frighten someone into doing what you want.
entries.definitionCN: 恐吓；胁迫（使人因害怕而服从）

entries.definition: To put someone or something in danger, with no suggestion of words.
entries.definitionCN: 危及（不含言语威胁之意）

entries.definition: To tell someone about a possible danger so they can avoid it.
entries.definitionCN: 警告（出于提醒，而非施压）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the -en verb pattern, the two main uses, and the passive form.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自 -en 动词规律、两种主要用法，以及被动式。

normal.en: Threaten is threat plus -en, the same way strength becomes strengthen.
normal.cn: threaten 就是 threat 加 -en，正如 strength 变成 strengthen。

normal.en: People threaten and things threaten: one with words, the other with pressure.
normal.cn: 人会威胁，物也会威胁：一个用言语，一个用压力。

normal.en: Threaten to rain is the sky making a promise it may not keep.
normal.cn: threaten to rain 是天空许下的一个未必兑现的承诺。

normal.en: Be threatened with closure means a job or a place is on the line.
normal.cn: be threatened with closure 意为一份工作或一个地方岌岌可危。

normal.en: The noun is threat; remember the verb carries the extra -en.
normal.cn: 名词是 threat；记住动词多带了 -en。

abstract.en: Picture a storm front pushing across the sky, pressing the whole town down before a drop falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一道雨锋推过天空，一滴雨未落就把整座城压住。

abstract.en: To threaten is to lean forward without stepping.
abstract.cn: threaten 是身体前倾，却不迈出那一步。

abstract.en: The verb gives danger a voice and a body: words at the door, water at the wall.
abstract.cn: 这个动词给危险一副嗓音和一具身体：门口的话语，墙外的水。

examples.en: The two firms threatened each other with lawsuits.
examples.cn: 两家公司互相威胁要打官司。

examples.en: Rising seas threaten these coastal farms.
examples.cn: 海面上升危及这些沿海农场。

examples.en: It threatened to snow all morning but never did.
examples.cn: 整个上午都像要下雪，却始终没下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死瑞腾」——死命拽着不放，逼得人腾不出身 → threaten 威胁

root: 名词 threat（日耳曼词根「压、挤」）加动词后缀 -en 构成，与 widen、strengthen 同型；由「出声施压」扩展为「以事物之势危及」，并衍生被动式「面临……威胁」。

sensesIntro.en: Threaten applies pressure in three voices: a person speaking harm, a force putting something at risk, and a sky that hints at what is coming.
sensesIntro.cn: threaten 以三种嗓音施加压力：人说出伤害、力量使某物处于险境、天空暗示即将来临之事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a storm front pressing across the sky before a single drop falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴雨未落就压过天空的雨锋。

branches.en: The voice: harm named out loud as leverage.
branches.cn: 嗓音线：把伤害说出口当作筹码。

branches.en: The force: smoke, water or heat doing the pressing.
branches.cn: 力量线：烟、水或热在施压。

branches.en: The sky: clouds that hint and never quite deliver.
branches.cn: 天空线：乌云暗示着，却往往落空。

branches.en: The institution: a library or a custom on the line.
branches.cn: 机构线：图书馆或习俗岌岌可危。

branches.en: Passive forms let anything be threatened, from health to a species.
branches.cn: 被动式让任何对象都能被威胁，从健康到物种。

intro.en: Threaten is a noun turned verb by -en, and the family adds -ing, -ed and -ly.
intro.cn: threaten 是由名词加 -en 转成的动词，词族再叠加 -ing、-ed 与 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Both the base and the suffix are native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 词基与后缀都属日耳曼本土，拉丁词条留空。

definition_zh: 三；三个
definition_en: the number equal to two plus one, coming after two and before four
core_image: 桌上摆着三只小碗，排成一个稳稳的三角形
scene: 早餐桌上摆着三只小碗,一只盛粥,一只装咸菜,一只放鸡蛋。There were three bowls on the table and one empty chair.
sceneCN: 这里 three 是「三、三个」（第 1 个义项：数量三个）；句意为桌上摆着三只碗，还有一把空椅子。

pos.zh: 三个一组；三号大小的东西

collocations.zh: 三分之一；三个人中有一个

derivatives.zh: 由本词加序数后缀构成，义为「第三；三分之一」
由本词演变来的数词，义为「十三」
由本词演变来的数词，义为「三十」
由本词加 -fold 构成，义为「三倍的；三重的」

senses.title: The number three
senses.definition: the number equal to two plus one, used to count people or things
senses.definitionCN: 等于二加一的数，用于计数
senses.example: She bought three apples and gave one to me.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了三个苹果，给了我一个。
senses.why: The number is one of the oldest words English has, and it simply counts.
senses.whyCN: 这个数词是英语最古老的词之一，用途就是计数。

senses.title: In groups of three
senses.definition: three things taken together as a set, often in the pattern in threes
senses.definitionCN: 三个合为一组，常用于 in threes 的格式
senses.example: The dancers moved in threes across the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者三人一组走过舞台。
senses.why: The plural turns a count into a pattern: three at a time, as others go in twos.
senses.whyCN: 复数把计数变成队形：三个一拨，就像别人两个一拨。

senses.title: Used in fixed expressions
senses.definition: used in phrases such as three times or one in three to express repetition, ratio or proportion
senses.definitionCN: 用于 three times、one in three 等短语，表示次数、倍数或比例
senses.example: One in three households in the survey owned a bicycle.
senses.exampleCN: 调查中每三户就有一户拥有自行车。
senses.why: Inside fixed phrases the bare number stops counting things and measures repetition or share.
senses.whyCN: 在固定短语里，这个光秃秃的数字不再数物，而是衡量重复次数与所占份额。

intro.en: Three is one of the oldest words in English, inherited straight from Germanic and from Indo-European.
intro.cn: three 是英语中最古老的词之一，直接从日耳曼语、再往上从印欧语继承而来。

items.en: The Germanic form was close to thriz, and its relatives are visible in German drei and Dutch drie.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式接近 thriz，其亲属见于德语 drei 与荷兰语 drie。

items.en: Old English þrī had a separate feminine form þrēo, because the old language agreed numbers with gender.
items.cn: 古英语 þrī 另有阴性形式 þrēo，因为古英语的数词要随名词的性变化。

items.en: Middle English merged the forms into three, and the old -r- of the Germanic form was lost in England.
items.cn: 中古英语把各种形式并为 three，日耳曼形式中原有的 -r- 在英格兰失落。

items.en: Modern English keeps three only in the plural form for most uses, and third as its ordinal.
items.cn: 现代英语多数场合只用 three，其序数词为 third。

items.en: Three keeps a strong cultural life in sayings, so it appears in rules of three and in lists.
items.cn: three 在谚语中生命力很强，常出现在「三分法则」与列举里。

note.en: The first group lines up the numerals built on three; the second compares neighbouring numbers and counting words.
note.cn: 第一组排开由 three 构成的数词；第二组比较相邻数字与计量词。

entries.definition: The ordinal of three, one of the few irregular -rd forms.
entries.definitionCN: 第三；少数以 -rd 结尾的不规则序数词

entries.definition: Ten plus three; the stress falls on the second syllable.
entries.definitionCN: 十三；重音在第二个音节

entries.definition: Three times ten; the stress falls on the first syllable.
entries.definitionCN: 三十；重音在第一个音节

entries.definition: A woody plant; it sounds almost the same but comes from another root.
entries.definitionCN: 树；读音几乎相同，词源不同

entries.definition: The number just before three.
entries.definitionCN: 二；三的前一个数

entries.definition: The number just after three.
entries.definitionCN: 四；三的后一个数

entries.definition: Consisting of three parts, or three times as much; from Latin.
entries.definitionCN: 三倍的；由三部分组成的（拉丁来源）

entries.definition: A group of three, usually of people or musicians.
entries.definitionCN: 三人组；三重奏（拉丁来源）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the numeral family and the fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自数词家族与固定短语。

normal.en: Third is the ordinal, and it is irregular, not threeth.
normal.cn: 序数词是 third，属不规则变化，不写 threeth。

normal.en: Thirteen and thirty both start from the old form of three.
normal.cn: thirteen 与 thirty 都从 three 的古形演变而来。

normal.en: In threes means the group size is three, like in twos.
normal.cn: in threes 意为三个一组，正如 in twos。

normal.en: One in three is the same as a third.
normal.cn: one in three 相当于三分之一。

normal.en: A three-year-old is written with hyphens before the noun.
normal.cn: three-year-old 放在名词前时要加连字符。

abstract.en: Picture three bowls on a table, a shape that stands steady without any support.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上三只碗，组成一个不需要支撑也稳当的形状。

abstract.en: Three is the first number that feels like a group, not just a pair.
abstract.cn: 三是第一个让人感到「成组」而不只是「成对」的数。

abstract.en: Beginning, middle and end: three is the smallest shape of a complete story.
abstract.cn: 开端、中间与结尾：三是完整故事最小的形状。

examples.en: Three of the windows were broken in the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨中有三扇窗户破了。

examples.en: The children lined up in threes for the walk.
examples.cn: 孩子们三人一组排好队去散步。

examples.en: One in three students rides a bike to school.
examples.cn: 每三个学生中有一个骑车上学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「事利」——三件事一起做才顺利，三人成众 → three 三

root: 英语本土最古老的基础词之一：日耳曼语 thriz → 古英语 þrī / 阴性 þrēo → 中古英语并为 three；序数词 third，另有 thirteen、thirty 等派生数词。

sensesIntro.en: Three counts items, groups them in sets of three, and serves inside fixed phrases of repetition and ratio.
sensesIntro.cn: three 用来数物、把物三个一组，也用在表示次数与比例的固定短语里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three bowls set out on a table in a steady triangle.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上三只碗，摆成一个稳当的三角形。

branches.en: The count: three of a thing.
branches.cn: 计数线：某物的三个。

branches.en: The set: three taken together as a group.
branches.cn: 成组线：三个合为一组。

branches.en: The phrase: three times, one in three.
branches.cn: 短语线：三次、三分之一。

branches.en: Counting and ratio share the same bare numeral.
branches.cn: 计数与比例共用同一个光秃秃的数词。

branches.en: Groups of three appear wherever people act together.
branches.cn: 三人一组出现在一切需要协作的场合。

intro.en: Three multiplies into thirteen and thirty and takes -fold and -s for derived forms.
intro.cn: three 衍生出 thirteen 与 thirty，并可加 -fold 与 -s 构成派生形式。

latinIntro.en: The word is inherited Indo-European, with no Latin source, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词是继承自印欧语的基础词，不经拉丁语，拉丁词条留空。

definition_zh: 兴旺；繁荣；茁壮成长；蓬勃发展
definition_en: to grow well and be healthy, or to be successful and continue growing strongly
core_image: 窗台上一盆绿植越过花盆边缘，越窜越高
scene: 小区角落原本光秃的墙根,如今爬山虎长得密密匝匝。The old brick wall is now covered with ivy that thrives in the damp shade.
sceneCN: 这里 thrive 是「茁壮成长」（第 2 个义项：植物长得旺盛）；句意为那面旧砖墙如今爬满了在潮湿阴处长得旺盛的常春藤。

collocations.zh: 在压力下反而表现出色

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「兴旺的；繁荣的」
本词的过去分词形式，义为「已兴旺起来」
与本词同源的近亲名词，义为「节俭」（语义已分化）

senses.title: To succeed and grow strong
senses.definition: to become successful, strong and healthy, of a business, city or person
senses.definitionCN: 指事业、城市或人变得成功、强健、健康
senses.example: The little bookshop thrived after it began hosting readings.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小书店开始办朗读会之后兴旺起来。
senses.why: The Norse verb meant to take a firm hold, so success is pictured as a grip that holds.
senses.whyCN: 这个北欧语动词意为「牢牢抓住」，因此成功被想象成一把抓稳的手。

senses.title: To grow vigorously, of plants
senses.definition: to grow strongly and healthily, especially of plants in favourable conditions
senses.definitionCN: 尤指植物在适宜条件下长得健壮旺盛
senses.example: These roses thrive in full sun and well-drained soil.
senses.exampleCN: 这些玫瑰在阳光充足、排水良好的土里长得很好。
senses.why: Applied to plants, the grip image becomes roots holding soil and shoots pushing up.
senses.whyCN: 用在植物上，抓握的意象就变成根系抓住土壤、枝条向上推送。

senses.title: To do well in difficult conditions
senses.definition: to do well because of conditions that would weaken others, used with on or under
senses.definitionCN: 因那些会削弱别人的条件而表现得更好，后接 on 或 under
senses.example: Some people thrive on a tight deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 有些人在紧迫的期限下反而状态极好。
senses.why: The preposition on marks the source: the pressure itself feeds the growth.
senses.whyCN: 介词 on 标出源头：压力本身成了生长的养分。

senses.title: To flourish culturally or socially
senses.definition: to develop strongly and spread, of ideas, arts or customs
senses.definitionCN: 指观念、艺术或习俗发展壮大并传播开来
senses.example: Coffee culture thrives in this part of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡文化在城市的这一带很盛行。
senses.why: Ideas are treated like plants: they take hold, spread and bloom across a place.
senses.whyCN: 观念被当作植物看待：它们落地、蔓延，在一个地方成片开花。

intro.en: Thrive comes from Old Norse, and its older meaning was to grasp or to seize, not to grow.
intro.cn: thrive 来自古北欧语，较早的意义是「抓住」，并非「成长」。

items.en: The Norse verb þrífask meant to prosper and also to grasp or take hold of something.
items.cn: 北欧语动词 þrífask 既表示「兴旺」，也表示「抓住、握住」。

items.en: The root behind it meant to grip or to press, the same pressure family that gives threat.
items.cn: 其背后的词根意为「抓紧、压住」，与 threat 同属压迫一族。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word from Norse settlers and used it for growing strong and prospering.
items.cn: 中古英语从北欧移民借入这个词，用来表示「长得强健」与「兴旺」。

items.en: Early modern English gave the word both a bodily and a commercial sense, a thriving plant and a thriving trade.
items.cn: 早期现代英语让它兼具身体与商业两面：茁壮的植物与兴隆的生意。

items.en: Modern English added the pattern thrive on, meaning to do better because of something.
items.cn: 现代英语发展出 thrive on 的用法，表示「因某事而更好」。

note.en: The first group gathers the thrive family and its Norse relatives; the second compares words of success and growth.
note.cn: 第一组收 thrive 词族及其北欧近亲；第二组比较表示成功与生长的词。

entries.definition: The adjective for a healthy, growing business or plant.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「兴旺的、繁荣的」

entries.definition: From the same Norse family, meaning careful management of money.
entries.definitionCN: 节俭（同源，语义已转向理财）

entries.definition: The adjective of thrift, meaning careful with money.
entries.definitionCN: 节俭的（thrift 的形容词）

entries.definition: Very exciting; the -ill- pattern is close but the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 令人激动的（-ill- 拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: To grow or develop very well, especially of plants and arts.
entries.definitionCN: 繁荣；茂盛（尤指植物与艺术）

entries.definition: To become successful, usually of money and business.
entries.definitionCN: 兴旺；致富（多指经济层面）

entries.definition: To open into flower, and figuratively to come into your own.
entries.definitionCN: 开花；焕发光彩

entries.definition: To dry up and fade, the exact opposite of thriving.
entries.definitionCN: 枯萎；衰败（thrive 的反义）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the Norse origin, the grip image, and the thrive on pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自北欧来源、「抓握」意象，以及 thrive on 句式。

normal.en: The old Norse verb meant to grab hold, and a plant that thrives has taken firm hold of its soil.
normal.cn: 古北欧语动词意为「抓住」，长得旺的植物正是抓住了土。

normal.en: Thrive on shows the pattern: the thing that would hurt others helps you.
normal.cn: thrive on 显示这种句式：会让别人受伤的东西反而帮了你。

normal.en: The past tense form throve is old style, and thrived is the everyday choice.
normal.cn: 过去式 throve 偏古，日常多用 thrived。

normal.en: Thrift comes from the same Norse family: both words are about making something go far.
normal.cn: thrift 出自同一条北欧语脉：两个词都关乎「让有限之物发挥到极致」。

normal.en: A thriving market and a thriving rose bush share one word.
normal.cn: 繁荣的市场与旺盛的玫瑰丛共用一个词。

abstract.en: Picture a vine that has found the one crack of light and climbed over the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一株藤找到了唯一的裂缝阳光，一路爬过墙头。

abstract.en: To thrive is not just to survive the winter but to burst out in spring.
abstract.cn: thrive 不只是熬过冬天，而是春天炸开般地生长。

abstract.en: The word makes growth look like a grip that keeps getting tighter.
abstract.cn: 这个词让成长看起来像一把越握越紧的手。

examples.en: Small firms thrive when rules are simple.
examples.cn: 规则简单时，小公司就能兴旺。

examples.en: These plants thrive in damp, shaded corners.
examples.cn: 这些植物在阴湿的角落里长得很好。

examples.en: She thrives on difficult problems.
examples.cn: 她越遇到难题越有劲头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踹五」——一脚踹开五道门槛，生意越踹越旺 → thrive 兴旺

root: 古北欧语 þrífask「兴旺；抓住」，与日耳曼语「抓紧、压住」词根同源（与 threat 同族）；中古英语借入后表示「长壮、兴旺」，现代又发展出 thrive on 的用法。

sensesIntro.en: Thrive keeps one image of taking a firm hold and lets it grow into business success, healthy plants, strength under pressure and living cultures.
sensesIntro.cn: thrive 保留「牢牢抓住」这一个意象，让它蔓生为事业成功、植物健壮、压力下的强韧与兴盛的文化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vine that has found the light and climbed over the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：找到阳光、一路爬过墙头的藤。

branches.en: The venture: businesses and people doing well.
branches.cn: 事业线：生意与人越来越好。

branches.en: The plant: roots that grip and shoots that climb.
branches.cn: 植物线：根系紧抓，枝条上扬。

branches.en: The strain: doing better exactly where others fail.
branches.cn: 压力线：恰在别人撑不住处表现出色。

branches.en: The culture: ideas and habits spreading and blooming.
branches.cn: 文化线：观念与习惯传播开来、开花结果。

branches.en: Commercial and botanical growth share one word.
branches.cn: 商业增长与植物生长共用一个词。

intro.en: Thrive stays simple; English adds -ing and the older irregular endings.
intro.cn: thrive 保持简单，英语在其上加 -ing 以及较老的不规则词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word comes through Old Norse with no Latin source, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词经古北欧语而来，没有拉丁语来源，拉丁词条留空。

definition_zh: 喉咙；咽喉；嗓门；窄口
definition_en: the passage at the back of the mouth that carries food to the stomach and air to the lungs
core_image: 一条细窄的通道，从口腔往里，食物和空气都要挤过这里
scene: 唱了整晚的歌,第二天早上他几乎说不出话来。My throat is so sore that I can hardly speak this morning.
sceneCN: 这里 throat 是「喉咙」（第 1 个义项：口腔后方的通道）；句意为今早我喉咙痛得几乎说不出话。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -y 构成，义为「喉音的；沙哑的」
由本词加 -ed 构成，多用于复合词，义为「有……喉的」

senses.title: The passage inside the neck
senses.definition: the front of the neck and the passage inside it, through which food and air pass
senses.definitionCN: 颈部前侧及其内部、食物与空气经过的通道
senses.example: He had a sore throat and stayed in bed all day.
senses.exampleCN: 他喉咙痛，一整天都待在床上。
senses.why: The root meant to swell, and the throat is the swollen-looking passage in the neck.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「膨胀」，喉咙就是颈中那条看上去鼓起的通道。

senses.title: The voice, informally
senses.definition: the voice, especially its quality or strength, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 指嗓音，尤指其音质或力度，多用于口语
senses.example: She has a good throat for singing folk songs.
senses.exampleCN: 她唱起民歌来有一副好嗓子。
senses.why: The passage that makes voice is easily named for the voice itself.
senses.whyCN: 造就声音的通道很容易被直接用来称呼声音本身。

senses.title: A narrow opening
senses.definition: a narrow entrance or passage, such as the throat of a bottle
senses.definitionCN: 狭窄的入口或通道，如瓶颈
senses.example: The throat of the bottle was too narrow for the brush.
senses.exampleCN: 瓶口太窄，刷子伸不进去。
senses.why: The body image is transferred outward: any narrow passage in an object is its throat.
senses.whyCN: 身体的意象被移到体外：任何器物的窄通道都是它的「喉」。

senses.title: The narrow land between areas
senses.definition: a narrow strip of land or water forming a passage between two larger areas
senses.definitionCN: 连接两片较大区域的狭长陆地或水道
senses.example: The valley is the throat of the northern trade routes.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山谷是北方商路的咽喉。
senses.why: The body image moves outward once more: narrow land between wide regions is a throat.
senses.whyCN: 身体意象再一次移到体外：宽广区域之间的狭长陆地也是一道咽喉。

intro.en: Throat comes from Old English, and the root behind it meant to swell, which describes the bulge of the neck.
intro.cn: throat 来自古英语，其词根意为「膨胀」，正是对颈部鼓起之形的描述。

items.en: The Germanic root for swelling or puffing up lies behind the word, a picture of the rising front of the neck.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中表示「膨胀、鼓起」的词根是其来源，正是颈前隆起之形。

items.en: Old English þrote named the front of the neck and the gullet, both the outside and the passage.
items.cn: 古英语 þrote 兼指颈前与外食管，内外两面都包括。

items.en: Middle English throat settled the spelling, and the word kept both the outer neck and the inner passage.
items.cn: 中古英语固定了 throat 的拼写，并保留颈外与颈内通道两义。

items.en: Modern English added the transferred use for narrow openings, from bottles to valleys.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了移用义，指从瓶口到山谷的各种窄口。

items.en: Idioms about clearing, cutting or forcing down the throat keep the body image alive in everyday speech.
items.cn: 关于清嗓、割喉、强灌的习语让这个身体意象在日常口语中一直鲜活。

note.en: The first group separates the throat family from its near spellings; the second compares body passages and narrow openings.
note.cn: 第一组区分 throat 词族与形近词；第二组比较身体通道与窄口。

entries.definition: Deep and rough in voice, as if from the throat.
entries.definitionCN: 喉音的；沙哑的

entries.definition: To send something through the air; it sounds the same at the start but has another root.
entries.definitionCN: 投掷；开头读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: Used in compounds such as white-throated, describing the throat of a bird.
entries.definitionCN: 用于 white-throated 一类复合词，描述鸟的喉部

entries.definition: From one side to the other; one letter shape apart from throat.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过；与 throat 拼写形近

entries.definition: The tube from the throat to the stomach; the medical word for the inner passage.
entries.definitionCN: 食管（喉到胃的管内通道，医学用词）

entries.definition: The voice box at the top of the throat.
entries.definitionCN: 喉；声带所在的器官

entries.definition: The whole part joining head and body, with the throat at its front.
entries.definitionCN: 脖子（咽喉位于其前面）

entries.definition: A valve controlling an engine, originally the throat of the pipe.
entries.definitionCN: 节流阀（原指管子的喉部，与 throat 同源）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the swelling root, the narrow-passage image and the idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自「膨胀」词根、窄通道意象，以及相关习语。

normal.en: The root meant to swell; the throat is the swelling front of the neck.
normal.cn: 词根意为「膨胀」；喉咙就是颈前鼓起的那部分。

normal.en: A sore throat is the everyday complaint that names the passage directly.
normal.cn: a sore throat 是最日常的说法，直接点名那条通道。

normal.en: Clear your throat, not your through: the two words look alike.
normal.cn: 是 clear your throat，不是 through：两个词长得像。

normal.en: Throttle shares the root: it was the throat of a pipe before it was a valve.
normal.cn: throttle 同源：它先是管子的喉部，后来才成了阀门。

normal.en: A bottle has a throat, and so does a mountain valley.
normal.cn: 瓶子有喉咙，山谷也有咽喉。

abstract.en: Picture everything going in and out of the body having to squeeze through one narrow gate.
abstract.cn: 想象进出身体的一切都必须挤过同一道窄门。

abstract.en: The word is the narrowness itself: inner passage, voice, bottle mouth or mountain pass.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是「窄」本身：内通道、嗓音、瓶口或山口。

abstract.en: Speak of the throat and you speak of the bottleneck of every body.
abstract.cn: 提到喉咙，就提到每具身体的瓶颈。

examples.en: He cleared his throat before beginning the speech.
examples.cn: 他清了下嗓子才开始讲话。

examples.en: A cold can leave you with a sore throat.
examples.cn: 感冒可能会让你喉咙痛。

examples.en: The boat slipped through the throat of the harbour.
examples.cn: 小船驶过了港口的咽喉水道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「思漏特」——一想到这里就紧张，喉咙漏风说不出话 → throat 喉咙

root: 古英语 þrote，源自日耳曼词根「膨胀、鼓起」，本指颈前隆起处及其内通道；今兼指嗓音、器物窄口与地形要隘，同源词 throttle 原即「管喉」。

sensesIntro.en: Throat is the body’s narrow gateway, and the same narrowness is lent to the voice, to bottles and to mountain passes.
sensesIntro.cn: throat 是身体的窄门，这份「窄」又被借给嗓音、瓶口与山口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: everything entering and leaving the body squeezing through one narrow gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：进出身体的一切都挤过同一道窄门。

branches.en: The body: the passage for air and food.
branches.cn: 身体线：空气与食物共用的通道。

branches.en: The sound: the throat standing for the voice.
branches.cn: 声音线：喉咙代指嗓音。

branches.en: The object: neck of a bottle, throat of a pipe.
branches.cn: 器物线：瓶颈、管喉。

branches.en: The landscape: a valley or strait as a passage.
branches.cn: 地形线：作为通道的山谷或海峡。

branches.en: Inside and outside narrowness share one image.
branches.cn: 体内的「窄」与器物的「窄」共用同一意象。

intro.en: Throat forms a -y adjective and takes -s; its older relative throttle already carries the narrow-throat image.
intro.cn: throat 可加 -y 构成形容词并加 -s，同源词 throttle 已带有「窄喉」意象。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词为日耳曼本土词，拉丁词条留空。

items.exampleCN: 它构成复合词里的 throated。

items.example: The larynx holds the vocal cords.

definition_zh: 穿过；通过；从头到尾；（时间）自始至终；凭借
definition_en: from one end or side of something to the other, by way of something, or during the whole of a period
core_image: 一条隧道笔直贯穿整座山，两头都见光
scene: 火车钻进隧道,十分钟后才从另一头钻出,眼前豁然开朗。The train went through the tunnel and came out into bright sunshine.
sceneCN: 这里 through 是「穿过」（第 1 个义项：从一端到另一端）；句意为火车穿过隧道，出来时是一片明亮的阳光。

pos.zh: 穿过；通过；凭借；自始至终
穿过；从头到尾；（电话）接通
直达的；完事的（英式口语）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 out 复合而成，义为「遍及；自始至终」
同根孪生词，由「贯穿到底」引申为「彻底的」
由 break 与 through 复合而成，义为「突破」

senses.title: From one side to the other
senses.definition: from one end, side or surface of something to the other
senses.definitionCN: 从某物的一端、一侧或一面到另一端
senses.example: The river runs through the centre of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河从镇中心穿过。
senses.why: The word is a preposition of motion built on a root for passing, and this is its oldest and most physical use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是由表示「通过」的词根构成的运动介词，这是它最古老、最具体的用法。

senses.title: By way of something
senses.definition: by means of, by way of, or from one person or thing to another
senses.definitionCN: 凭借、经由，或从一个人或事物传到另一个
senses.example: She got the job through a friend at the company.
senses.exampleCN: 她通过公司里的一位朋友得到了这份工作。
senses.why: A path through a place becomes a means through a system: the physical route turns into a channel.
senses.whyCN: 穿过某地的路变成穿过某体系的途径：实体路线转为渠道。

senses.title: During the whole of a period
senses.titleCN: 自始至终；贯穿整个时期
senses.definition: from the beginning to the end of a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 从某段时间的开头到结尾
senses.example: The shop stayed open through the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店整个假期都开门。
senses.why: Space and time share the image: a period is crossed the way a tunnel is crossed.
senses.whyCN: 空间与时间共用这个意象：跨越一段时间就像穿过一条隧道。

senses.title: Finished, or completed
senses.definition: finished with something, especially in the phrase be through with
senses.definitionCN: 完成某事，尤用于 be through with 短语
senses.example: Are you through with the computer? I need it.
senses.exampleCN: 你用完了电脑吗？我要用。
senses.why: To be through an object is to have come out the other side, so the work is behind you.
senses.whyCN: 穿过某物意味着已从另一侧出来，工作因此被留在身后。

senses.title: Connected by phone
senses.definition: connected to the person you want on the telephone, in the phrase get through
senses.definitionCN: 在电话中联系上要找的人，用于 get through
senses.example: I tried several times but could not get through.
