senses.exampleCN: 我试了好几次都没接通。
senses.why: A call travels through the network until it reaches someone, so connecting is getting through.
senses.whyCN: 通话穿过网络抵达某人，因此接通就是 get through。

intro.en: Through is one of the oldest prepositions in English, from a Germanic root for passing across.
intro.cn: through 是英语最古老的介词之一，源自表示「穿过」的日耳曼词根。

items.en: The root meant to go over or through, a picture of a door or gate being crossed.
items.cn: 词根意为「越过、穿过」，是穿过门或关口的画面。

items.en: Old English þurh was a preposition of motion and means, used both for space and for agency.
items.cn: 古英语 þurh 既是运动介词也表手段，兼指空间与施事。

items.en: Middle English through absorbed Norse influence and settled the initial thr- spelling and pronunciation.
items.cn: 中古英语 through 受北欧语影响，固定了 thr- 的拼写与读音。

items.en: The adjective thorough split off early, taking over the sense of complete, and the adverb throughout was built with out.
items.cn: 形容词 thorough 很早就分离出去，接管「彻底」义，副词 throughout 则由 out 复合而成。

items.en: Modern English extends through to time and to communication, so a call and a holiday can both be got through.
items.cn: 现代英语把 through 扩展到时间与通信，于是电话与假期都能「过」。

note.en: The first group separates through from its spelling neighbours and relatives; the second compares prepositions of movement.
note.cn: 第一组区分 through 与形近、同族词；第二组比较表示运动的介词。

entries.definition: The adjective for complete and careful, split off from the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底的（与 through 同源后分化）

entries.definition: Through plus out, meaning in every part or the whole of a period.
entries.definitionCN: 遍及；自始至终（through + out）

entries.definition: The concessive conjunction; it differs in vowel and voice.
entries.definitionCN: 虽然（元音与清浊音都不同）

entries.definition: To excite strongly; the opening looks similar but the root differs.
entries.definitionCN: 使兴奋；开头形近，词源不同

entries.definition: From one side to the other of a surface, rather than an inside.
entries.definitionCN: 横过（强调面而非内部）

entries.definition: Following the length of something, not crossing it.
entries.definitionCN: 沿着（顺着长度，非横穿）

entries.definition: By way of; a Latin word for routing and means.
entries.definitionCN: 经由；通过（正式）

entries.definition: With the help of; a formal phrase for instrument and method.
entries.definitionCN: 借助；通过（正式短语）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the pass-through root, the twin thorough, and the compound throughout.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自「穿过」词根、孪生词 thorough，以及复合词 throughout。

normal.en: Through and thorough are twins: one crosses, the other has crossed right to the end.
normal.cn: through 与 thorough 是双胞胎：一个在穿，一个已经穿到底。

normal.en: Throughout is through plus out, covering every part.
normal.cn: throughout 就是 through 加 out，覆盖每一部分。

normal.en: Through can cross time: all through the night is a tunnel made of hours.
normal.cn: through 能穿过时间：all through the night 是一条由小时组成的隧道。

normal.en: Get through on the phone means the call has crossed the network to a person.
normal.cn: get through 意为通话穿过网络到达了人。

normal.en: Do not write it as though: that word means although.
normal.cn: 不要写成 though：那是「虽然」。

abstract.en: Picture a tunnel crossing a mountain with light at both ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一条贯穿山体的隧道，两头都有光。

abstract.en: Space, time and method are all tunnels the word digs.
abstract.cn: 空间、时间与方法，都是这个词挖出的隧道。

abstract.en: To be through something is to have left it behind.
abstract.cn: be through 某物，就是把它留在了身后。

examples.en: We walked through the old market on the way home.
examples.cn: 回家路上我们穿过老市场。

examples.en: He worked through the night to finish the design.
examples.cn: 他通宵赶完了设计。

examples.en: I got the news through a colleague.
examples.cn: 我是通过一位同事得知这个消息的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「出路」——找到出路就是穿过去 → through 穿过

root: 古英语 þurh，源自日耳曼语「越过、穿过」词根，同源孪生词 thorough 后分化出「彻底」义；throughout 由 through + out 复合而成。

sensesIntro.en: Through digs one tunnel and drives it through space, method, time, a finished task and a phone line.
sensesIntro.cn: through 只挖一条隧道，却把它打通了空间、手段、时间、完成的任务与电话线路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tunnel crossing a mountain, light at both ends.
core.cn: 核心意象：贯穿山体、两头见光的隧道。

branches.en: The place: right through the middle.
branches.cn: 空间线：从正中穿过。

branches.en: The channel: through a friend, through hard work.
branches.cn: 渠道线：通过朋友、通过努力。

branches.en: The stretch: through the night, through the year.
branches.cn: 时段线：通宵、整年。

branches.en: The ending: through a task, through to a caller.
branches.cn: 终点线：做完了事，接通了电话。

branches.en: Space and time use one and the same image.
branches.cn: 空间与时间共用同一个意象。

intro.en: Through compounds productively: throughout, breakthrough, and the split-off adjective thorough.
intro.cn: through 能构成许多复合词：throughout、breakthrough，以及分化出去的 thorough。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词为日耳曼本土词，拉丁词条留空。

items.meaning: in every part; all the time

items.exampleCN: 该厂的吞吐量翻了一番。

items.meaning: from one side to the other

definition_zh: 遍及；贯穿整个；自始至终
definition_en: in every part of a place or thing, or during the whole of a period of time
core_image: 一盏灯从屋顶照下来，屋里每个角落都被照亮
scene: 这座城市从南到北都在下雨,骑车的人个个罩着雨衣。Rain fell throughout the city, from the harbour to the northern hills.
sceneCN: 这里 throughout 是「遍及、贯穿整个」（第 1 个义项：空间上的每一处）；句意为整座城市从港口到北边山地都在下雨。

forms.label: 无变化（介词与副词同形）

derivatives.zh: 复合中的前一部分，义为「穿过」
复合中的后一部分，义为「向外、全部」
同根孪生词，义为「彻底的」

senses.title: In every part of a place
senses.definition: in or into every part of a place, area or object
senses.definitionCN: 在某地、某区域或某物体的每一部分中
senses.example: The fire alarm could be heard throughout the building.
senses.exampleCN: 整栋楼都能听见火警铃声。
senses.why: Through supplies the passage and out supplies the spread, so the word covers every part of a space.
senses.whyCN: through 提供「贯穿」，out 提供「铺开」，于是这个词覆盖了一个空间的每一部分。

senses.title: During the whole of a period
senses.titleCN: 自始至终；贯穿整个时期
senses.definition: during the whole of a period of time, from beginning to end
senses.definitionCN: 在某段时间的整个过程中，从头到尾
senses.example: She remained calm throughout the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 整个面试过程中她都保持镇定。
senses.why: Time is crossed the same way a space is: the compound reaches both ends of the period.
senses.whyCN: 时间与空间以同样的方式被穿过：这个复合词抵达这段时间的两端。

senses.title: In all parts of a group or field
senses.definition: in every part of a group, field or body of work
senses.definitionCN: 在某个群体、领域或全部作品中的每一处
senses.example: The idea appears throughout his early novels.
senses.exampleCN: 这个想法贯穿他早期的小说。
senses.why: A body of work is treated like a place, and the idea is found in every part of it.
senses.whyCN: 一批作品被当作一个地方，而这个想法在其中每一处都能找到。

senses.title: As a standalone adverb
senses.definition: used alone, especially after a noun, to mean in every part or the whole time
senses.definitionCN: 单独作副词，尤用于名词之后，表示「处处」或「一直」
senses.example: The house was painted white throughout.
senses.exampleCN: 这所房子里里外外都刷成了白色。
senses.why: With no noun after it, the compound simply means all over, in space or in time.
senses.whyCN: 后面不接名词时，这个复合词就单纯表示「到处、始终」，用于空间或时间。

intro.en: Throughout is a plain English compound of through and out, first recorded in the Old English period.
intro.cn: throughout 是 through 与 out 构成的朴实英语复合词，最早见于古英语时期。

items.en: The compound of þurh and ūt already meant on every side or entirely, built the same way as other out compounds.
items.cn: þurh 与 ūt 的复合在古英语已表示「四面八方、完全」，与其他带 out 的复合词构词相同。

items.en: Middle English throughout kept both the spatial sense and the temporal one, and settled as a single word.
items.cn: 中古英语 throughout 兼有空间与时间两义，并固定为一个词。

items.en: Early modern English added the extended use for groups and works, as in throughout his writings.
items.cn: 早期现代英语增添了用于群体与作品的引申用法，如 throughout his writings。

items.en: Modern English uses throughout more in writing than in speech, where all through is often preferred.
items.cn: 现代英语里 throughout 多用于书面，口语更常用 all through。

items.en: The adverb use without a following noun remains common, as in painted white throughout.
items.cn: 不接名词的副词用法依然常见，如 painted white throughout。

note.en: The first group unpacks the compound and its relatives; the second compares prepositions of extent.
note.cn: 第一组拆解这个复合词及其亲属；第二组比较表示范围的介词。

entries.definition: From one side to the other; the first half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过；复合词的前半

entries.definition: The everyday spoken equivalent, common before a period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 口语常用说法，多接时间段

entries.definition: Complete and careful; the adjective twin of through.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底的（through 的形容词孪生词）

entries.definition: Covering every part of a place; the loose spoken partner of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 遍布；本词的口语松散对应说法

entries.definition: In every place; it cannot take a noun after it.
entries.definitionCN: 到处（后不能接名词）

entries.definition: Covering the whole of a surface or place, often informally.
entries.definitionCN: 遍布（多用于口语）

entries.definition: From one side to the other, or over the whole of an area.
entries.definitionCN: 横跨；遍及

entries.definition: Through the course of a period; it does not mean everywhere in a place.
entries.definitionCN: 在……期间（不含空间「遍及」义）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the two parts of the compound and from its written register.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自复合词的两个部分，以及它的书面语体。

normal.en: Throughout is through plus out: passing through, then spread out everywhere.
normal.cn: throughout 就是 through 加 out：先穿过，再铺开到各处。

normal.en: Use it for places and for periods, but not for a point in time.
normal.cn: 它用于地点与时段，不用于某个时间点。

normal.en: In speech, all through often does the same job.
normal.cn: 口语里 all through 常干同样的活。

normal.en: The adverb use takes no noun: white throughout means white all over.
normal.cn: 副词用法不接名词：white throughout 意为里外全白。

normal.en: Mind the noun after it: throughout the city, not throughout city.
normal.cn: 注意后面要有冠词或限定词：throughout the city。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp hung from the ceiling, reaching the corners the floor lamp misses.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏吊灯挂在天花板上，照到了落地灯照不到的角落。

abstract.en: The word stretches a space or a period until nothing outside it remains.
abstract.cn: 这个词把一个空间或一段时间拉长，直到外面什么都不剩。

abstract.en: It is the quiet, written cousin of everywhere.
abstract.cn: 它是 everywhere 那个安静的书面对应词。

examples.en: The festival is celebrated throughout the country.
examples.cn: 这个节日在全国各地都庆祝。

examples.en: He kept notes throughout the lecture.
examples.cn: 整场讲座他都在记笔记。

examples.en: The walls were painted pale grey throughout.
examples.cn: 墙里里外外都刷成了浅灰色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「出路熬特」——出路熬到特别久，一路贯彻到底 → throughout 自始至终

root: 古英语由 þurh（through，穿过）+ ūt（out，向外）复合而成，表示「四面八方、完全」，后兼指时间自始至终，并引申用于群体与作品。

sensesIntro.en: Throughout stretches the tunnel image over a space, a period, a body of work, or the whole of an object.
sensesIntro.cn: throughout 把隧道意象拉伸到一片空间、一段时间、一批作品，或一个物体的整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp hung high, lighting every corner at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：高悬的灯，一次照亮每个角落。

branches.en: The space: every room, every region.
branches.cn: 空间线：每间屋、每个地区。

branches.en: The period: from beginning to end.
branches.cn: 时段线：从开头到结尾。

branches.en: The field: across a whole body of ideas or novels.
branches.cn: 领域线：贯穿全部想法或小说。

branches.en: The object: white throughout, without a noun.
branches.cn: 物体线：white throughout，不带名词。

branches.en: Place and time are stretched by the same compound.
branches.cn: 空间与时间由同一个复合词拉满。

intro.en: Throughout is itself a compound; it does not take further endings.
intro.cn: throughout 本身已是复合词，不再加其他词尾。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are native English, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都是英语本土词，拉丁词条留空。

definition_zh: 扔；投掷；抛；（使）陷入（某种状态）；举办
definition_en: to send something through the air with your hand, or to cause someone to be in a particular state
core_image: 手臂向后一拉，手腕一甩，东西划出一道弧线飞出去
scene: 院子里父子俩来回扔着球,球在阳光下划出一道又一道弧线。The father threw the ball high and the boy ran to catch it.
sceneCN: 这里 throw 是「扔、抛」（第 1 个义项：用手把东西投向空中）；句意为父亲把球高高扔起，男孩跑过去接住。

pos.zh: 使陷入（某种状态）；使困惑
举办（聚会）；投射（光线、影子）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -er 构成，义为「投掷者；（机器）抛掷装置」
由 throw 与 away 复合，义为「用完即弃的；随口说出的话」
由 throw 与 back 复合，义为「复古之物；返祖现象」

senses.title: To send something through the air
senses.definition: to send something through the air with your hand, using a quick movement of the arm
senses.definitionCN: 用手臂快速动作把东西送向空中
senses.example: He threw the keys across the table to me.
senses.exampleCN: 他把钥匙隔着桌子扔给我。
senses.why: The root meant to twist or turn, and the arm turns as it hurls something away.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「扭、转」，手臂在甩出东西时正是扭转的。

senses.title: To make someone be in a state
senses.definition: to cause someone or something to be suddenly in a particular state or situation
senses.definitionCN: 使人或事物突然进入某种状态或处境
senses.example: The news threw the whole office into confusion.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息让整个办公室陷入混乱。
senses.why: A blow of feeling hurls a mind the way a hand hurls a stone.
senses.whyCN: 情绪的打击把心甩出去，就像手甩出一块石头。

senses.title: To shine or cast light and shadow
senses.definition: to send light or shadow onto a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把光或影投到某表面上
senses.example: The low sun threw long shadows across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 低斜的太阳在田野上投下长长的影子。
senses.why: Light and shadow are thrown like objects: they travel from the source and land on a surface.
senses.whyCN: 光与影像物体一样被抛出：从源头飞出，落在表面上。

senses.title: To hold a party or event
senses.definition: to organise and hold a party, dinner or similar social event
senses.definitionCN: 组织和举办聚会、晚宴等社交活动
senses.example: They threw a party for her return.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为她的归来办了一场聚会。
senses.why: A party is launched the way an object is thrown: set in motion and let go.
senses.whyCN: 聚会像物体一样被抛出：先使它动起来，再松手放手。

senses.title: To be pushed off a horse or in a fight
senses.definition: to make a rider fall from a horse, or to make someone fall in a fight
senses.definitionCN: 使骑手从马上摔下，或在搏斗中把对方摔倒
senses.example: The horse threw its rider at the first fence.
senses.exampleCN: 那匹马在第一道栅栏处把骑手摔了下来。
senses.why: The rider is thrown off, the same physical hurl applied to a person.
senses.whyCN: 骑手被甩了下来，还是那同一次物理的投掷，只是对象换成了人。

intro.en: Throw is a native English verb from a root meaning to twist or turn, the same family as thread.
intro.cn: throw 是英语本土动词，源自意为「扭、转」的词根，与 thread 同族。

items.en: The root meant to twist or turn round, which describes the motion of an arm hurling something.
items.cn: 词根意为「扭、转」，正描述手臂甩出东西的动作。

items.en: Old English þrāwan meant to twist or turn, and only later took on the sense of hurling through the air.
items.cn: 古英语 þrāwan 意为「扭、转」，后来才获得「抛向空中」之义。

items.en: Middle English throw covered casting, hurling and even throwing a rider, and the noun throw appeared beside it.
items.cn: 中古英语 throw 兼指投、掷，乃至把骑手摔下，旁生名词 throw。

items.en: Modern English added abstract and social uses: to throw light on a question, to throw a party.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了抽象与社交用法：throw light on a question、throw a party。

items.en: The phrasal patterns, throw away and throw up, gave the verb a large second life in everyday speech.
items.cn: throw away 与 throw up 这类短语搭配，让这个动词在日常口语中获得了极大的第二生命。

note.en: The first group gathers the throwing family and near spellings; the second compares verbs of sending things outward.
note.cn: 第一组收投掷词族与形近词；第二组比较表示「送出」的动词。

entries.definition: The past tense, sounding like through but meaning threw.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式；读音与 through 相同

entries.definition: The past participle, used after have or be.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词

entries.definition: A person or machine that throws.
entries.definitionCN: 投掷者；抛掷装置

entries.definition: From one side to the other; the same sound as threw.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过；与 threw 同音

entries.definition: To throw lightly or carelessly, often upward.
entries.definitionCN: 轻抛；随手扔（常向上）

entries.definition: To throw with great force, often in anger.
entries.definitionCN: 猛掷（带力量与怒气）

entries.definition: To throw with a sudden, wild movement.
entries.definitionCN: 猛甩；乱扔

entries.definition: To throw or send out, especially light, a shadow or a vote.
entries.definitionCN: 投；投射（正式，常用于光、影、票）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the twisting root, the irregular forms and the phrasal uses.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自「扭、转」词根、不规则变化，以及短语搭配。

normal.en: Throw, threw, thrown: the vowel shifts from -ow to -ew to -own, like grow and blow.
normal.cn: throw, threw, thrown：元音从 -ow 变 -ew 再到 -own，与 grow、blow 相同。

normal.en: Thrown is the past participle; threw is only for the simple past.
normal.cn: thrown 是过去分词；threw 只用于一般过去时。

normal.en: The root meant to twist, and your arm twists as it throws.
normal.cn: 词根意为「扭」，手臂在扔出时正是扭转的。

normal.en: Throw light on means to make a problem clear, as if light were thrown at it.
normal.cn: throw light on 意为让问题变清楚，就像把光投在上面。

normal.en: Throw a party does not mean throwing anything away: it means holding one.
normal.cn: throw a party 不是把聚会扔掉，而是举办聚会。

abstract.en: Picture a stone leaving the hand in a curve, the arm still turning behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象石头以弧线离手，手臂还在身后转动。

abstract.en: The verb sends not just objects but light, shadows and states of mind.
abstract.cn: 这个动词送出的不只是物体，还有光、影与心境。

abstract.en: Everything thrown is briefly free of the hand that held it.
abstract.cn: 被抛出的一切，都短暂地离开了托着它的手。

examples.en: She threw the ball back over the fence.
examples.cn: 她把球扔回栅栏那边。

examples.en: The report throws new light on the accident.
examples.cn: 这份报告让事故有了新的解释。

examples.en: They threw a party when the project was finished.
examples.cn: 项目完成后他们办了一场聚会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「思入」——把思虑一股脑扔进风里 → throw 扔

root: 古英语 þrāwan，源自日耳曼词根「扭、转」（与 thread 同族），本义「扭转」，后转指以扭转的手臂抛掷；由物理投掷引申出投射光影子、使人陷入状态、举办活动等义。

sensesIntro.en: Throw begins as an arm twisting something into the air and then throws light, shadows, states of mind and even parties.
sensesIntro.cn: throw 起初是手臂一扭把东西甩向空中，后来也抛出光、影、心境，乃至一场聚会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone leaving the hand in a curve, the arm still turning.
core.cn: 核心意象：石头以弧线离手，手臂仍在转动。

branches.en: The object: keys, a ball, a stone.
branches.cn: 物体线：钥匙、球、石头。

branches.en: The abstract throw: feelings and shadows flung outward.
branches.cn: 抽象线：情绪与影子被甩出去。

branches.en: The social throw: a party organised and launched.
branches.cn: 社交线：聚会从筹办到开启。

branches.en: The violent throw: a rider off a horse.
branches.cn: 暴力线：骑手被摔下马。

branches.en: Hand and emotion share one hurling verb.
branches.cn: 手与情绪共用同一个「甩」的动词。

intro.en: Throw takes -er for the doer, and it compounds with away and back.
intro.cn: throw 加 -er 表施事者，并与 away、back 构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词为日耳曼本土词，拉丁词条留空。

items.meaning: a return to an older type

items.example: Project the image on the wall.

definition_zh: 猛推；插入；推力；要旨
definition_en: to push something or someone suddenly and strongly, or the strong forward force that does this
core_image: 手掌平贴，一瞬间把东西直直地推出去
scene: 人群忽然向前一挤,他被推得差点撞到栏杆上。The crowd thrust him forward against the barrier.
sceneCN: 这里 thrust 是「猛推」（第 1 个义项：突然而有力地推）；句意为人群把他猛推向前，撞上了围栏。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -er 构成，义为「推进器；推的人」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「有进取心的；向外突出的」

senses.title: To push suddenly and hard
senses.definition: to push something or someone suddenly and with force
senses.definitionCN: 突然而有力地推某物或某人
senses.example: He thrust the letter into my hand and walked off.
senses.exampleCN: 他把信硬塞到我手里就走了。
senses.why: The word comes from the Norse verb for pressing, and its first job is still the physical shove.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自北欧语中表示「压、推」的动词，最基本的用途仍是实体的猛推。

senses.title: To force something on someone
senses.definition: to make someone accept an idea, duty or position whether they want it or not
senses.definitionCN: 不管对方愿不愿意，迫使其接受想法、责任或职位
senses.example: The decision was thrust upon the small team at the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定在最后一刻被硬塞给这个小团队。
senses.why: The shove becomes social: a duty is pressed onto someone who never asked for it.
senses.whyCN: 这一推变成了社会性的：一项责任被压到从没要过它的人身上。

senses.title: The force that pushes forward
senses.definition: the strong forward force made by an engine, a swimmer or an arm
senses.definitionCN: 发动机、游泳者或手臂产生的强向前之力
senses.example: The rocket’s thrust lifted it clear of the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 火箭的推力把它推离地面。
senses.why: The noun turns the push into a measurable force, always pointing forward.
senses.whyCN: 名词把这一推变成可计量的力，方向始终向前。

senses.title: The main point of an argument
senses.definition: the main idea or aim of a plan, argument or policy
senses.definitionCN: 计划、论证或政策的主要想法或目标
senses.example: The main thrust of the report is that costs must fall.
senses.exampleCN: 报告的要旨是必须削减开支。
senses.why: An argument pushes a reader in one direction, and that direction is its thrust.
senses.whyCN: 论证把读者推向一个方向，那个方向就是它的要旨。

intro.en: Thrust came into English from Old Norse, a cousin of throw, and both share a pressing, twisting root.
intro.cn: thrust 经古北欧语进入英语，与 throw 是表亲，两者共有「压、扭」的词根。

items.en: The root carried both twisting and pressing, so the arm both turns and pushes.
items.cn: 这个词根兼含「扭」与「压」两重意味，于是手臂既转又推。

items.en: Norse þrýsta meant to press or compel, and Norse settlers brought it into English use.
items.cn: 北欧语 þrýsta 意为「压、逼迫」，由北欧移民带入英语。

items.en: Middle English used thrust for a strong push and for forcing something on someone, as in thrust into.
items.cn: 中古英语用 thrust 表示强力推动，也用于 thrust into 这类「硬塞」的表达。

items.en: The noun appeared with the machine age, naming the forward force of engines and rockets.
items.cn: 名词义随机械时代出现，用来命名发动机与火箭的向前推力。

items.en: Modern English keeps an abstract sense as well, the thrust of an argument or a policy.
items.cn: 现代英语还保留抽象义，指论证或政策的要旨。

note.en: The first group gathers the thrust family and near spellings; the second compares verbs of pushing.
note.cn: 第一组收 thrust 词族与形近词；第二组比较表示推的动词。

entries.definition: An engine or device that produces thrust.
entries.definitionCN: 推进器；产生推力的装置

entries.definition: To hurl through the air; a close relative with a long-o vowel.
entries.definitionCN: 扔；同族近亲，元音不同

entries.definition: Careful use of money; similar thri- opening, different root.
entries.definitionCN: 节俭；开头相似，词源不同

entries.definition: To rely on someone; one vowel apart and differently rooted.
entries.definitionCN: 信任；只差一个元音，词源不同

entries.definition: The general verb for pressing forward; plain and neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 推（最普通的说法，语气中性）

entries.definition: To push roughly, often with the hands, and informally.
entries.definitionCN: 猛推；粗暴地推（偏口语）

entries.definition: To drive or push something forward, usually of engines.
entries.definitionCN: 推进（正式，多指机械）

entries.definition: To force forward or to make someone act; also the noun for motivation.
entries.definitionCN: 驱动；驱使（也作名词表示驱动力）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the Norse pressing origin and the three-way sense split.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自北欧语「压」的来源，以及三路引申的分叉。

normal.en: Thrust, thrust, thrust: the past form never changes, like cut and put.
normal.cn: thrust 的过去式与过去分词都不变化，与 cut、put 一样。

normal.en: The verb comes from a Norse word for pressing, so it is a push with weight behind it.
normal.cn: 动词源自北欧语表示「压」的词，因此这一推背后带着分量。

normal.en: A rocket’s thrust is a push you cannot see but can feel.
normal.cn: 火箭的 thrust 是看不见却能感到的推。

normal.en: The thrust of an argument is where the argument is pushing you.
normal.cn: 论证的 thrust 就是它在往哪个方向推你。

normal.en: Thrust upon means the duty was pushed onto you without asking.
normal.cn: thrust upon 意为责任被不问一声就压到你身上。

abstract.en: Picture a flat palm in one instant pushing a door all the way open.
abstract.cn: 想象一只平掌在一瞬间把门推到底。

abstract.en: One word serves the hand, the engine and the argument.
abstract.cn: 同一个词服务于手、引擎与论证。

abstract.en: Thrust is force with a direction: no pushing in circles.
abstract.cn: thrust 是有方向的力：不绕着圈推。

examples.en: She thrust the note into her pocket and ran.
examples.cn: 她把便条塞进口袋就跑。

examples.en: The engine’s thrust is measured in newtons.
examples.cn: 发动机的推力以牛顿为单位计量。

examples.en: The thrust of his speech was a call for patience.
examples.cn: 他演讲的要旨是呼吁耐心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死拉斯特」——死命拉着还顺手一推，力量十足 → thrust 猛推

root: 古北欧语 þrýsta「压、逼迫」进入英语，与 throw 同族，共享日耳曼词根「压、扭」；由实体猛推延伸出「强加」「（机械）推力」与「要旨」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Thrust is one strong directional push, applied by a hand, a duty, a rocket or an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: thrust 就是一次有力的定向推压，施加者可以是手、一项责任、一枚火箭或一段论证。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat palm pushing a door open in one instant.
core.cn: 核心意象：平掌在一瞬间把门推到底。

branches.en: The hand: a letter shoved into a palm.
branches.cn: 手线：把信塞进掌心。

branches.en: The burden: a duty pushed onto someone.
branches.cn: 负担线：责任被推到某人身上。

branches.en: The machine: newtons of forward force.
branches.cn: 机械线：以牛顿计的向前之力。

branches.en: The argument: the direction a report pushes you.
branches.cn: 论证线：报告把你推向的方向。

branches.en: Body and engine share the same straight-line force.
branches.cn: 身体与引擎共用同一股直线之力。

intro.en: Thrust takes -er for the doer or device and -ing for the adjective and noun.
intro.cn: thrust 加 -er 表示施事者或装置，加 -ing 表示形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: The word came through Old Norse with no Latin source, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词经古北欧语而来，没有拉丁语来源，拉丁词条留空。

items.meaning: one who pushes or a device

definition_zh: 拇指；竖起拇指表示赞许；（用拇指）翻阅
definition_en: the short thick finger at the side of the hand, or to press and turn pages with it
core_image: 一只手摊开，粗短的拇指单独朝上立着
scene: 旧书店里,他站在架前随手一页页翻过去,看有没有笔记。He thumbed through the old book, looking for notes in the margins.
sceneCN: 这里 thumb 作动词，是「用拇指翻阅」（第 3 个义项：飞快地翻动书页）；句意为他翻着这本旧书，找页边有没有笔记。

pos.zh: 用拇指翻（书页）；竖起拇指示意搭车

derivatives.zh: 由 thumb 与 nail 复合，义为「拇指甲；缩略图」
由 thumb 与 print 复合，义为「拇指印」
由 thumbs 与 up 复合，义为「赞许的表示」

senses.title: The short thick finger
senses.definition: the short thick finger at the side of the hand, able to touch the other fingers
senses.definitionCN: 手侧粗短、能与其他手指相触的手指
senses.example: She held the coin between her thumb and forefinger.
senses.exampleCN: 她用拇指和食指夹住那枚硬币。
senses.why: The root meant to swell, and the thumb is the swollen-looking finger on the side of the hand.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「膨胀」，拇指就是手侧那根看上去鼓短的手指。

senses.title: The gesture of approval
senses.definition: in the phrase thumbs up or thumbs down, a sign of approval or rejection
senses.definitionCN: 用于 thumbs up 或 thumbs down，表示赞成或反对
senses.example: The project got a thumbs up from the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目得到了委员会的认可。
senses.why: The finger that can point up or down carries the whole vote in a gesture.
senses.whyCN: 那根能朝上也能朝下的手指，用一个手势承包了整场投票。

senses.title: To turn pages with the thumb
senses.definition: to press the pages of a book and turn them quickly, reading only briefly
senses.definitionCN: 用拇指压住书页快速翻动，只看个大概
senses.example: He thumbed through the magazine while he waited.
senses.exampleCN: 他一边等一边翻看那本杂志。
senses.why: The thumb both holds the book open and flicks the pages, so it became the verb for skimming.
senses.whyCN: 拇指既按住书页又拨动书页，于是成了「快速翻阅」的动词。

senses.title: A rough rule from experience
senses.definition: in the phrase rule of thumb, a rough method based on practice rather than theory
senses.definitionCN: 用于 rule of thumb，指凭实践而非理论得出的粗略方法
senses.example: As a rule of thumb, allow one hour for every site.
senses.exampleCN: 按经验，每个地点留一小时。
senses.why: A thumb’s width was once a handy measure, and a rough measure turned into a rough rule.
senses.whyCN: 一个拇指宽曾是方便的尺度，而粗略的尺度就变成了粗略的规则。

intro.en: Thumb is a native English word from a root meaning to swell, the same idea behind thick.
intro.cn: thumb 是英语本土词，源自意为「膨胀」的词根，与 thick「厚」同出一源。

items.en: The root described swelling or thickening, a good fit for the short, fat finger.
items.cn: 这个词根描述「膨胀、变厚」，正适合形容那根又短又粗的手指。

items.en: Old English þūma named the thumb, and the final -b appeared later under the influence of words like limb.
items.cn: 古英语 þūma 指拇指，末尾的 -b 是后来受 limb 一类词影响才出现的。

items.en: Middle English speakers used the thumb in everyday measure, so expressions of skill and clumsiness grew around it.
items.cn: 中古英语时期人们以拇指作日常尺度，关于灵巧与笨拙的说法便围绕它生出。

items.en: The verb thumb through, marking pages with the thumb, appeared once reading became common.
items.cn: 动词 thumb through 指用拇指标记书页，是阅读普及后才出现的。

items.en: Modern English keeps thumbs up in messages and images as well as in gesture.
items.cn: 现代英语让 thumbs up 既留在手势里，也进入消息与图片。

note.en: The first group gathers the thumb compounds and near spellings; the second compares finger words and gestures.
note.cn: 第一组收 thumb 的复合词与形近词；第二组比较手指类词与手势表达。

entries.definition: The nail of the thumb, and hence a very small picture.
entries.definitionCN: 拇指甲；引申为缩略图

entries.definition: The mark left by a thumb, used for identification.
entries.definitionCN: 拇指印（用于身份辨认）

entries.definition: The gesture or signal of approval, written with a hyphen.
entries.definitionCN: 表示赞许的手势或信号，带连字符

entries.definition: To hit heavily with a dull sound; one letter from thumb, other root.
entries.definitionCN: 重击（与 thumb 差一个字母，词源不同）

entries.definition: Any of the four long digits; the thumb is not counted among them in English.
entries.definitionCN: 手指（英语中拇指通常不计入 finger）

entries.definition: The finger next to the thumb, used for pointing.
entries.definitionCN: 食指（紧邻拇指、用于指物）

entries.definition: A digit of the foot, the body part parallel to the thumb.
entries.definitionCN: 脚趾（与手指对应的部位）

entries.definition: To move something with a quick movement of the finger or thumb.
entries.definitionCN: 轻弹（用指或拇指快速拨动）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the swelling root, the silent -b and the compound words.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自「膨胀」词根、不发音的 -b，以及复合词。

normal.en: The b at the end is silent, so thumb sounds exactly like thum.
normal.cn: 末尾的 b 不发音，thumb 读起来就是 thum。

normal.en: The root meant to swell, and the thumb is the swollen finger.
normal.cn: 词根意为「膨胀」，拇指就是那根鼓起来的手指。

normal.en: Thumbs up and thumbs down need the plural -s even for one thumb.
normal.cn: thumbs up 和 thumbs down 即使指一只拇指也用复数 -s。

normal.en: All thumbs means the hands feel like fat thumbs: clumsy.
normal.cn: all thumbs 意为手上像全是粗拇指：笨手笨脚。

normal.en: Thumbnail is a thumb’s nail and, later, a tiny picture.
normal.cn: thumbnail 本是拇指甲，后来指小图。

abstract.en: Picture the short fat finger standing up alone while the rest fold away.
abstract.cn: 想象那根粗短的手指独自竖起，其余全收起来。

abstract.en: A thumb can measure, turn a page, hitch a lift and say yes.
abstract.cn: 一根拇指能量高矮、翻书页、搭便车，还能说「行」。

abstract.en: The clumsiest finger is also the one that shows approval.
abstract.cn: 最笨拙的手指，也是用来表示赞许的手指。

examples.en: He gave me a quick thumbs up through the window.
examples.cn: 他隔着窗户朝我快速比了个拇指。

examples.en: She thumbed through the report before the meeting.
examples.cn: 开会前她飞快地翻了一遍报告。

examples.en: As a rule of thumb, one cup of rice serves two people.
examples.cn: 按经验，一杯米够两个人吃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「萨姆」——萨姆总是竖起拇指夸人 → thumb 拇指

root: 古英语 þūma，源自日耳曼词根「膨胀、变厚」，与 thick 同源；末尾 -b 为后加。由拇指实体引申出竖拇指表态、用拇指翻页及「经验法则」等用法。

sensesIntro.en: Thumb starts as the swollen finger and then earns its keep in gestures, in page-turning and in practical rules.
sensesIntro.cn: thumb 起初是那根「鼓起的手指」，此后靠手势、翻页与经验法则立住脚跟。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the short fat finger standing up alone while the others fold away.
core.cn: 核心意象：粗短的手指独自竖起，其余手指全收起来。

branches.en: The body part: a finger that can touch all its neighbours.
branches.cn: 身体线：能碰到其他所有手指的那一根。

branches.en: The sign: up for yes, down for no.
branches.cn: 手势线：向上为赞，向下为否。

branches.en: The action: pages flipped under the thumb.
branches.cn: 动作线：被拇指拨动的书页。

branches.en: The rule: a width of thumb as a rough guide.
branches.cn: 规则线：以拇指宽作粗略尺度。

branches.en: The hand measures as easily as it gestures.
branches.cn: 手既能打手势，也能当尺子。

intro.en: Thumb compounds with nail, print and up, and takes ordinary verb endings.
intro.cn: thumb 可与 nail、print、up 复合，动词则加普通词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词为日耳曼本土词，拉丁词条留空。

items.example: He is thumbing through a map.

items.meaning: a cap worn on the thumb
items.meaningCN: 顶针（原是戴在拇指上的）

definition_zh: 雷；雷声；轰隆声；怒吼
definition_en: the loud noise that follows lightning in a storm, or any very loud rolling sound
core_image: 乌云压顶，一道白光之后整片天空轰隆隆地滚过
scene: 夏夜的雨来得急,雷声在孩子头顶滚过,他一下子钻进被子里。The thunder rolled across the valley and the child hid under the blanket.
sceneCN: 这里 thunder 是「雷声」（第 1 个义项：雷雨中紧随闪电的巨大声响）；句意为雷声滚过山谷，孩子躲进了被子里。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ous 构成，义为「雷鸣般的；轰响的」
由 thunder 与 storm 复合，义为「雷暴」
由 thunder 与 bolt 复合，义为「霹雳；雷电」
由本词加 -y 构成，义为「有雷的；闷热欲雷的」

senses.title: The noise after lightning
senses.definition: the loud rolling noise heard after a flash of lightning during a storm
senses.definitionCN: 雷雨中闪电之后听到的巨大滚响
senses.example: A clap of thunder woke the whole house.
senses.exampleCN: 一声炸雷惊醒了整幢房子。
senses.why: Thor, the hammer-wielding god of storms, hides in the first syllable of this word.
senses.whyCN: 手持锤子的雷神托尔（Thor）就藏在这个词的第一个音节里。

senses.title: Any loud rolling sound
senses.definition: a very loud, deep and continuing noise made by traffic, water, applause or a crowd
senses.definitionCN: 车辆、水流、掌声或人群发出的响亮而低沉的连续声响
senses.example: The thunder of the waterfall could be heard a mile away.
senses.exampleCN: 瀑布的轰鸣声一英里外就能听到。
senses.why: Any sound as deep and continuous as a storm borrows the storm’s name.
senses.whyCN: 凡是像风暴那样低沉而持续的声音，都可以借用风暴的名字。

senses.title: To make a loud rolling noise
senses.definition: to make a loud deep noise, or for the sky to sound with thunder
senses.definitionCN: 发出响亮低沉的声响，或指天上打雷
senses.example: The trucks thundered past on the old bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车在老桥上一路轰隆而过。
senses.why: The verb keeps the physical roar: heavy things moving with a rolling noise.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留实体的轰鸣：沉重之物带着滚动之声前进。

senses.title: To shout angrily
senses.definition: to speak very loudly and angrily, often of a person in authority
senses.definitionCN: 大声而愤怒地说话，多指有权威的人
senses.example: The coach thundered at the players to get back in line.
senses.exampleCN: 教练对球员怒吼，叫他们排好队。
senses.why: A human voice raised to storm volume takes the same word.
senses.whyCN: 人声抬到风暴的音量，就用同一个词。

intro.en: Thunder is named after Thor, the Germanic god of storms, and the word has kept his hammer in its sound.
intro.cn: thunder 取自日耳曼雷神 Thor 之名，读音里还留着那把锤子的分量。

items.en: The common Germanic word for the storm god was Thunraz, borrowed as Thor in Norse and Thunor in Old English.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中雷神之名为 Thunraz，北欧语作 Thor，古英语作 Thunor。

items.en: Old English þunor was both the god and the noise he was thought to make, so the natural sound and the god shared one name.
items.cn: 古英语 þunor 既是神，也是人们认为神发出的响声，自然之声与神共用一个名字。

items.en: When the speaker d moved into the word, the spelling thunder fixed the modern form and the god faded from it.
items.cn: 插入了 d 音之后，拼写 thunder 固定下来，神的身影也跟着隐去。

items.en: Modern English extends thunder to engines, crowds and waterfalls, and the verb to angry speech.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到引擎、人群与瀑布，动词则扩用于愤怒的说话。

items.en: Idioms such as steal someone’s thunder still remember a storm that can be taken away.
items.cn: steal someone’s thunder 一类习语，仍记得那场可以被夺走的风暴。

note.en: The first group gathers the thunder family and near spellings; the second compares loud natural sounds.
note.cn: 第一组收 thunder 词族与形近词；第二组比较自然界的大声响。

entries.definition: The adjective, as in thunderous applause.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，如「雷鸣般的掌声」

entries.definition: A storm with thunder and lightning.
entries.definitionCN: 雷暴；雷雨

entries.definition: A flash of lightning with a crash, and a sudden shock.
entries.definitionCN: 霹雳；晴天霹雳

entries.definition: Beneath something; it hides inside thunder but has a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 在……下面（藏在 thunder 之中，词源不同）

entries.definition: The flash of electricity in a storm; it comes before the thunder.
entries.definitionCN: 闪电（雷雨中的电光，先于雷声）

entries.definition: A low continuous sound, often further away and weaker than thunder.
entries.definitionCN: 隆隆声（常更远、更弱）

entries.definition: A very loud deep sound made by a lion, crowd, engine or sea.
entries.definitionCN: 咆哮；轰鸣（多由狮、人群、引擎或海发出）

entries.definition: A short deep explosive sound, like a drum.
entries.definitionCN: 低沉的爆响（短促，如鼓声）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the god Thor, the silent-looking d and the storms the word names.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自雷神 Thor、看起来「多出来」的 d，以及它命名的各种风暴。

normal.en: Thor is the thunder god, and his name is the first four letters.
normal.cn: Thor 是雷神，他的名字就是这个词的前四个字母。

normal.en: The d was added by speakers, so thunder sounds nothing like its spelling suggests.
normal.cn: 这个 d 是口语里后加的，读音与拼写差得很远。

normal.en: Thunder follows lightning; the light comes first and the sound arrives later.
normal.cn: thunder 跟在 lightning 之后：先见光，后闻声。

normal.en: Thunderous applause has nothing to do with storms but the volume.
normal.cn: 雷鸣般的掌声与风暴无关，只是音量相似。

normal.en: Steal someone’s thunder means to take the credit before they can speak.
normal.cn: steal someone’s thunder 意为抢在别人开口前抢走功劳。

abstract.en: Picture a whole sky rolling over like a heavy barrel down a stone road.
abstract.cn: 想象整片天空像一只重桶在石路上滚过。

abstract.en: The same word names the weather, applause and an angry voice.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既命名天气，也命名掌声与怒声。

abstract.en: Thunder is the sound of something enormous happening out of sight.
abstract.cn: thunder 是某件巨大之事在视野之外发生时的响动。

examples.en: Thunder rolled over the hills all evening.
examples.cn: 整个傍晚雷声都在山间滚动。

examples.en: The audience gave the singer thunderous applause.
examples.cn: 观众给歌手送上了雷鸣般的掌声。

examples.en: The waves thundered against the harbour wall.
examples.cn: 海浪轰隆隆地拍打着港口墙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「散得」——满天闷响一时散得干干净净 → thunder 雷声

root: 古英语 þunor，源自日耳曼雷神之名 Thunraz（北欧语 Thor），一词兼指雷神与其轰鸣；中古英语插入 d 音定型为 thunder，后引申为一切轰响与怒吼。

sensesIntro.en: Thunder begins as the voice of the storm god and spreads to every deep, rolling noise, from engines to angry coaches.
sensesIntro.cn: thunder 起初是雷神的声音，后来扩散到一切低沉滚动的巨响，从引擎到怒吼的教练。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole sky rolling over like a barrel on stone.
core.cn: 核心意象：整片天空像桶滚石路一般碾压而过。

branches.en: The weather: a storm’s deep voice.
branches.cn: 天气线：风暴的低沉嗓音。

branches.en: The world: waterfalls, lorries and applause.
branches.cn: 世界线：瀑布、卡车与掌声。

branches.en: The action: a sky or engine that thunders.
branches.cn: 动作线：天空或引擎在轰响。

branches.en: The voice: authority raised into a roar.
branches.cn: 人声线：权威抬高成咆哮。

branches.en: Storm and machinery borrow each other’s volume.
branches.cn: 风暴与机械互相借用彼此的音量。

intro.en: Thunder takes -ous and -y, and compounds with storm and bolt.
intro.cn: thunder 可加 -ous、-y，并与 storm、bolt 复合。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, though -ous and -y are borrowed endings that English applies freely.
latinIntro.cn: 词干为日耳曼语，-ous 与 -y 是英语借入后自由使用的后缀。

items.meaning: a lightning flash with a crash

definition_zh: 因此；从而；如此；这样
definition_en: as a result of what has just been said, or in this particular way
core_image: 前一段铺好的砖，正好接上后一段的路
scene: 报告最后一页写着一行结论,前面所有数据都往这一句收。Costs fell and sales rose; thus the year ended in profit.
sceneCN: 这里 thus 是「因此」（第 1 个义项：表示结果）；句意为成本下降、销量上升，因此这一年最终盈利。

derivatives.zh: 英语本土副词后缀 -ly 加于 thus，义同 thus，较罕见、语体偏随意
同属古英语指示词族，义为「到那边」

senses.title: As a result
senses.definition: used to introduce a result or conclusion that follows from what has just been said
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出由前文推出的结果或结论
senses.example: The roads were flooded; thus we stayed at home.
senses.exampleCN: 道路被淹了，因此我们待在家里。
senses.why: The word began as the instrumental form of the old demonstrative, literally by that means.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原是古老指示代词的工具格形式，字面就是「以那种方式」。

senses.title: In this way
senses.definition: in the way that has just been described or shown
senses.definitionCN: 以刚才描述或示范的方式
senses.example: Hold the tool thus, with the blade away from you.
senses.exampleCN: 这样握工具，让刀口朝向你之外的方向。
senses.why: The demonstrative origin survives most plainly here: exactly this way, often with a gesture.
senses.whyCN: 指示来源在这里最直白：正是这个方式，常配一个示范动作。

senses.title: So much, as in thus far
senses.definition: in phrases such as thus far, meaning up to this point
senses.definitionCN: 用于 thus far 等短语，意为「到此为止、到目前为止」
senses.example: Thus far the plan has worked well.
senses.exampleCN: 到目前为止，这个计划运行良好。
senses.why: Paired with far, the word sets a limit at the present moment.
senses.whyCN: 与 far 连用时，这个词把界限划在此刻。

senses.title: Formal marker of reasoning
senses.definition: used in formal writing to link a step of reasoning to the next
senses.definitionCN: 在正式书面语中连接推理步骤
senses.example: Thus the argument arrives at its first conclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 论证由此得出第一个结论。
senses.why: In print the word became a standard hinge between one step of reasoning and the next.
senses.whyCN: 在书面语中，这个词成了推理步骤之间标准的铰链。

intro.en: Thus is the old instrumental form of the demonstrative stem seen in this and that, so it means by this or that means.
intro.cn: thus 是 this、that 所用指示词干的古老工具格形式，本义就是「以这个／那个方式」。

items.en: The demonstrative stem pointed at things and also supplied a form meaning by that means.
items.cn: 指示词干既用于指物，也提供一个表示「以那种手段」的形态。

items.en: Old English þus meant in this way, and þȳs a comparative form meant by that means, hence therefore.
items.cn: 古英语 þus 意为「这样」，比较形式 þȳs 意为「以那种手段」，即「因此」。

items.en: Middle English merged the two, and thus came out with both its manner and its result sense.
items.cn: 中古英语把两者合并，thus 于是兼有方式与结果两义。

items.en: Print formalised the use of thus as a connective in arguments and official documents.
items.cn: 印刷文本使 thus 固定为论证与公文中的连接词。

items.en: Modern speech usually prefers so or therefore in its place, and thus reads as formal.
items.cn: 现代口语多用 so 或 therefore 取代它，thus 读来正式。

note.en: The first group gathers thus with its demonstrative relatives; the second compares result and manner connectors.
note.cn: 第一组把 thus 与它的指示类亲属放在一起；第二组比较结果与方式连接词。

entries.definition: The same meaning, built with -ly; it is uncommon and often humorous.
entries.definitionCN: 同义变体，加 -ly，罕见且常带戏谑

entries.definition: To that place, from the same old demonstrative stem.
entries.definitionCN: 到那边（同属古老指示词族）

entries.definition: The thing here; the same stem, now a determiner.
entries.definitionCN: 这（同一词干，现作限定词）

entries.definition: The thing there; the same stem, now a determiner.
entries.definitionCN: 那（同一词干，现作限定词）

entries.definition: As a result, marked by logic; the standard formal alternative.
entries.definitionCN: 因此（逻辑结果，标准的正式替代词）

entries.definition: The everyday spoken connector for result.
entries.definitionCN: 所以（口语常用）

entries.definition: For this reason, and often with a later time meaning as well.
entries.definitionCN: 因此；此后（正式）

entries.definition: As a result, with a slightly heavier formal tone.
entries.definitionCN: 因此；结果（正式，语气稍重）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the demonstrative stem and the register of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自指示词干与这个词的语体。

normal.en: Thus belongs to this and that: by this way, by that way.
normal.cn: thus 与 this、that 同族：以这个方式、以那个方式。

normal.en: In arguments it means therefore; in instructions it means in this way.
normal.cn: 在论证中它是「因此」，在说明里它是「这样」。

normal.en: Thus far means up to now, and it is a phrase fixed in formal writing.
normal.cn: thus far 意为「到目前为止」，是正式书面语的固定说法。

normal.en: In speech, swap it for so if you want to sound natural.
normal.cn: 口语里想自然些，就用 so 替换它。

normal.en: Thusly exists but is rare and sounds almost like a joke.
normal.cn: thusly 确实存在，但罕见，听起来几乎像玩笑。

abstract.en: Picture a row of bricks already laid, and the next one fitting exactly into the gap.
abstract.cn: 想象一排砖已铺好，下一块正好嵌进缝里。

abstract.en: The word is a bridge built out of the sentence before it.
abstract.cn: 这个词是用前一句搭起的桥。

abstract.en: One little word carries a whole chain of reasoning across.
abstract.cn: 一个小词把一整条推理链渡过河去。

examples.en: The printer jammed, and thus the report was late.
examples.cn: 打印机卡住了，报告因此迟到。

examples.en: Fold the cloth thus, with the pattern inside.
examples.cn: 把布这样折，花纹朝里。

examples.en: Thus far, none of the tests have failed.
examples.cn: 到目前为止，没有一项测试失败。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「自斯」——自此如此，由此得出结论 → thus 因此；如此

root: 古英语 þus「这样」与工具格 þȳs「以那种方式」在中古英语合并为 thus，源自与 this、that 相同的指示词干，故兼有「如此」与「因此」两义。

sensesIntro.en: Thus carries two old functions at once: the manner reading, in this way, and the result reading, therefore.
sensesIntro.cn: thus 同时承担两种古老功能：方式义的「这样」，以及结果义的「因此」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bricks already laid, with the next one fitting into the gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：砖已铺好，下一块正好嵌进缝里。

branches.en: The result: what follows from the last sentence.
branches.cn: 结果线：由前一句推出的事实。

branches.en: The manner: exactly this way, often with a demonstration.
branches.cn: 方式线：正是这样，常配示范动作。

branches.en: The limit: thus far, up to here.
branches.cn: 界限线：thus far，到这里为止。

branches.en: The register: a formal bridge in written reasoning.
branches.cn: 语体线：书面推理中的正式桥接。

branches.en: Manner and result are two faces of one old form.
branches.cn: 方式与结果是同一个古老形式的两面。

intro.en: Thus takes almost no endings; the -ly variant thusly is rare.
intro.cn: thus 几乎不加词尾，加 -ly 的 thusly 很罕见。

latinIntro.en: The word is native English, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词为英语本土词，拉丁词条留空。

items.exampleCN: 到目前为止我们意见一致。

definition_zh: 票；入场券；罚单；（政党）候选人名单
definition_en: a piece of paper or a digital pass that gives you the right to travel, enter or attend something
core_image: 一张印着几行小字的小纸片，检票口看一眼就放行
scene: 出门赶车前他忽然在口袋里翻找,怕那张小纸片弄丢了。She checked her pocket twice to make sure the ticket was still there.
sceneCN: 这里 ticket 是「车票」（第 1 个义项：凭以乘车的小票据）；句意为她摸了两次口袋，确认车票还在。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「售票；开罚单」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「持票的；被开罚单的」
由 ticket 与 holder 复合，义为「持票人」

senses.title: A pass for travel or entry
senses.definition: a printed or digital piece of evidence giving the holder the right to travel or enter
senses.definitionCN: 纸质或电子凭证，持者有乘车或入场的权利
senses.example: Two return tickets to the city, please.
senses.exampleCN: 请给我两张到城里的往返票。
senses.why: The word began as a written note, and a note is enough to pass a gate.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是一张书面便条，而一张便条足以通过一道闸。

senses.title: A notice of a fine
senses.definition: an official notice that you must pay a fine for a traffic or parking offence
senses.definitionCN: 因交通或停车违章而须缴纳罚款的正式通知
senses.example: There was a parking ticket under the windscreen wiper.
senses.exampleCN: 雨刷下夹着一张违章停车罚单。
senses.why: The right to pass became a right to punish: the same slip of paper, in another colour.
senses.whyCN: 「准予通行」变成了「予以处罚」：同一张小纸片，换了个颜色。

senses.title: A means to an end
senses.definition: in phrases such as a ticket to success, the thing that enables you to reach a goal
senses.definitionCN: 用于 a ticket to success 一类短语，指使人达到目标的手段
senses.example: Fluent English was her ticket to a better job.
senses.exampleCN: 流利的英语是她得到更好工作的门径。
senses.why: Whatever lets you through a door is a ticket, even when it is not paper.
senses.whyCN: 凡是能让你通过一道门的东西都是 ticket，即使它不是纸。

senses.title: A political list of candidates
senses.definition: the list of candidates that a party puts forward in an election
senses.definitionCN: 政党在选举中推出的候选人名单
senses.example: He won a place on the party ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 他赢得了该党名单上的一个位置。
senses.why: Candidates travel on one list as passengers travel on one ticket.
senses.whyCN: 候选人同上一个名单，就像乘客凭同一张票同行。

intro.en: Ticket came into English from French, where it began as a short note rather than a travel pass.
intro.cn: ticket 经法语进入英语，最初指一张短小的便条，而非车票。

items.en: Old French estiquet meant a note or a label, something stuck onto a document or a door.
items.cn: 古法语 estiquet 意为便条或标签，是贴在文书或门上的东西。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word as ticket, and it named a written note, a licence or a short record.
items.cn: 中古英语借入作 ticket，指书面便条、许可证或简短记录。

items.en: By the seventeenth century ticket had become the slip that admits you to a coach, a play or a lottery draw.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，ticket 已指让人乘车、看戏或抽签的凭据。

items.en: The nineteenth century added the police sense, the ticket that charges rather than admits.
items.cn: 十九世纪增添了警察用法：不再放行而是处罚的票单。

items.en: Modern English made tickets digital, but the word still means the right to go through.
items.cn: 现代英语让票数字化了，但这个词仍表示「可以过去」的权利。

note.en: The first group separates ticket from near spellings; the second compares passes, vouchers and fines.
note.cn: 第一组区分 ticket 与形近词；第二组比较票证、凭单与罚款。

entries.definition: A check mark, or a small insect; one syllable less and another root.
entries.definitionCN: 勾；蜱虫（少一个音节，词源不同）

entries.definition: To touch lightly and make someone laugh.
entries.definitionCN: 挠痒；使发笑

entries.definition: The rise and fall of the sea; a different root entirely.
entries.definitionCN: 潮汐；词源完全不同

entries.definition: An adhesive label, literally a thing stuck on.
entries.definitionCN: 贴纸（同源，本义「贴上去的东西」）

entries.definition: A card or document that lets you enter freely, often repeatedly.
entries.definitionCN: 通行证；定期票

entries.definition: A printed piece of paper exchangeable for goods or money.
entries.definitionCN: 代金券；凭单

entries.definition: The money paid for a journey, not the paper itself.
entries.definitionCN: 车费（指钱而非票）

entries.definition: Money paid as a penalty; the ticket is only the notice of it.
entries.definitionCN: 罚款（票只是通知，钱才是罚）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the short-note origin and the two opposite jobs of the same slip.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自「便条」的来源，以及同一纸片两种相反的职责。

normal.en: Ticket began as a little note, and a note still gets you through a gate.
normal.cn: ticket 最初是一张小便条，而一张便条仍能让你过闸。

normal.en: A travel ticket lets you go; a parking ticket stops you with a fine.
normal.cn: 车票放你过去，罚单则用罚款拦住你。

normal.en: Ticket office is where you pay before, the ticket machine where you pay quickly.
normal.cn: ticket office 是提前买票的地方，ticket machine 是快速买票的机器。

normal.en: A ticket to success is not paper; it is whatever opens the door.
normal.cn: 通往成功的 ticket 不是纸，而是任何能开门的凭据。

normal.en: Do not mix it with tick or tide: check the middle letters.
normal.cn: 不要与 tick 或 tide 混：看清中间的字母。

abstract.en: Picture a small slip flicked across a counter, the one thing that decides whether you pass.
abstract.cn: 想象一张小纸片从柜台那头弹过来，它单单决定你能不能过去。

abstract.en: The word is a legal token: it carries permission in miniature.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一枚微型的法律凭证，把许可装在小尺寸里。

abstract.en: The same paper can open a door or close a bank account.
abstract.cn: 同一张纸可以打开一扇门，也可以掏空一个账户。

examples.en: I booked two tickets for the evening train.
examples.cn: 我订了两张晚班火车的票。

examples.en: He got a ticket for parking on the pavement.
examples.cn: 他因为人行道上停车被开了罚单。

examples.en: Good writing is still a ticket to better work.
examples.cn: 好文笔仍是通往更好工作的门径。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「替课特」——替人上课特批一张凭条 → ticket 票

root: 古法语 estiquet「便条、标签」，中古英语借入为 ticket，本指书面便条或许可；十七世纪转指乘车看戏的凭据，十九世纪又衍生出交警罚单义。

sensesIntro.en: Ticket is a small slip that carries permission, and the same shape of paper can also carry a penalty, a career chance or a party list.
sensesIntro.cn: ticket 是一张承载许可的小纸片，同一形状的纸也能承载罚款、职业机会或政党名单。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small slip flicked across a counter that decides whether you pass.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张从柜台弹来的小纸片，决定你能不能过去。

branches.en: The pass: permission in miniature.
branches.cn: 通行线：微缩的许可。

branches.en: The fine: the same slip turned against you.
branches.cn: 罚款线：同一纸片反过来对付你。

branches.en: The chance: whatever opens a door.
branches.cn: 机会线：任何能开门的凭据。

branches.en: The list: candidates travelling together on one ballot.
branches.cn: 名单线：候选人共用一张选票同行。

branches.en: Two opposite powers share one small piece of paper.
branches.cn: 两种相反的权力共住一张小纸片。

intro.en: Ticket takes -s, -ed and -ing; it compounds with office, holder and machine.
intro.cn: ticket 可加 -s、-ed、-ing，并与 office、holder、machine 复合。

latinIntro.en: The stem came through French from an old root for sticking, with no Latin entry needed here.
latinIntro.cn: 词干经法语而来，源出表示「粘贴」的古老词根，此处无需拉丁词条。

definition_zh: 潮；潮汐；潮流；趋势
definition_en: the regular rise and fall of the sea, or a strong tendency in events or opinion
core_image: 海水沿着沙滩一点点爬上来，又悄悄退回去
scene: 退潮后的滩涂上留下一个个小水洼,孩子们踩着水找螃蟹。At low tide the children searched the wet sand for crabs.
sceneCN: 这里 tide 是「潮、潮汐」（第 1 个义项：海水的定期涨落）；句意为退潮时孩子们在湿沙里找螃蟹。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -al 构成，义为「潮汐的；潮水的」
由 tide 与 water 复合，义为「潮水；（美国）滨海地区」
形式相近但词源不同的名词，义为「消息」，勿混

senses.title: The rise and fall of the sea
senses.definition: the regular rise and fall of the sea caused by the pull of the moon and sun
senses.definitionCN: 由日月引力引起的海水定期涨落
senses.example: The tide comes in quickly along this beach.
senses.exampleCN: 这片海滩涨潮很快。
senses.why: The sea sense grew from the phrase tide of the sea, the scheduled time of the water.
senses.whyCN: 海洋义从 tide of the sea 这一说法长出来，指海水按时涨落。

senses.title: A tendency in events or opinion
senses.definition: a strong and changing tendency of events, opinion or fortune
senses.definitionCN: 事件、舆论或运势强烈而正在变化的走向
senses.example: The tide of opinion turned against the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 舆论的潮流转而对这个计划不利。
senses.why: Opinion rises and falls like water, so the sea image is used for events and fortune.
senses.whyCN: 舆论像水一样涨落，于是海洋意象被用于事态与运势。

senses.title: A period of time, in old use
senses.definition: an old word for a season or a period of time, surviving now mostly in compounds
senses.definitionCN: 古时表示季节或时段的词，现多存于复合词中
senses.example: In the tide of spring, the fields are all green.
senses.exampleCN: 春时田野一片翠绿。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, a season or fixed period, still visible in eventide and Yuletide.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的意义——季节或固定时段，在 eventide 与 Yuletide 中仍可见到。

senses.title: In the phrase tide over
senses.definition: in the phrasal verb tide over, to help someone through a difficult period
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语动词 tide over，帮助某人度过困难时期
senses.example: This loan will tide us over until the payment arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔贷款能帮我们撑到款项到账。
senses.why: In tide over, the sea image becomes help: the money keeps you floating until the water calms.
senses.whyCN: 在 tide over 中，海洋意象变成援手：这笔钱让你一直浮着，直到水面平静。

intro.en: Tide once meant simply time, and the sea sense grew out of the phrase tide of the sea.
intro.cn: tide 本义只是「时间」，海洋义是从「海的时间」这一说法里长出来的。

items.en: The root meant to divide or to stretch out, and gave a word for a fixed portion of time.
items.cn: 词根意为「划分、延展」，由此产生了表示「一段固定时间」的词。

items.en: Old English tīd meant time, season or hour, and appears in many compounds as a season word.
items.cn: 古英语 tīd 意为时间、季节或时辰，常作季节词出现在复合词中。

items.en: Middle English used the phrase tide of the sea for the scheduled rise and fall, and tide alone took on the sea sense.
items.cn: 中古英语用 tide of the sea 指按时涨落的潮水，tide 单用也逐渐取得海洋义。

items.en: The older time sense survives in compounds such as eventide and Yuletide, and in the word tidings.
items.cn: 较古的时间义保存在 eventide、Yuletide 这类复合词以及 tidings 之中。

items.en: Modern English extends tide to opinion and fortune, so a political tide can turn like a real one.
items.cn: 现代英语把 tide 扩展到舆论与运势，政治潮流也能像真潮水一样转向。

note.en: The first group gathers tide with its family and near spellings; the second compares movements of water and of events.
note.cn: 第一组把 tide 与词族、形近词放在一起；第二组比较水的运动与事态走向。

entries.definition: The adjective, as in tidal waters or tidal power.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，如「潮水」「潮汐能」

entries.definition: News or information, from the old sense of time and event, not from the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 消息（源自古老的「时间、事件」义，与海无关）

entries.definition: A pass or a fine; close in spelling and completely different in root.
entries.definitionCN: 票；罚单（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: A flat piece for covering roofs or floors.
entries.definitionCN: 瓦；瓷砖（词源不同）

entries.definition: A steady flow of water, air or opinion; it stresses direction and flow.
entries.definitionCN: 水流；潮流（强调方向与流动）

entries.definition: A moving ridge on water; one crest rather than the whole cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 波浪（单个波峰，非整个涨落周期）

entries.definition: The general direction of change, mostly of data and opinion.
entries.definitionCN: 趋势（多指数据与舆论的变化方向）

entries.definition: A period of the year; it inherits the older time sense of tide.
entries.definitionCN: 季节（继承 tide 更早的「时段」义）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the original time meaning and the sea image it grew into.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自原初的「时间」义及其长出的海洋意象。

normal.en: Tide used to mean time, and the sea keeps time twice a day.
normal.cn: tide 本义是时间，而海每天按时间涨落两回。

normal.en: Eventide and Yuletide still carry the old time meaning.
normal.cn: eventide 与 Yuletide 还保留着古老的时间义。

normal.en: Turn the tide is the picture of a battle turning like water at the shore.
normal.cn: turn the tide 就像战局像岸边水一样转向。

normal.en: Tide over means to float someone across a hard stretch.
normal.cn: tide over 意为把某人浮着渡过一段难关。

normal.en: Tidings is not the sea: it is news, from the old sense.
normal.cn: tidings 与海无关：它是消息，出自旧义。

abstract.en: Picture water climbing the sand and then slowly giving it back.
abstract.cn: 想象海水爬上沙滩，又缓缓把沙还给岸。

abstract.en: The word lets politics borrow the rhythm of the moon.
abstract.cn: 这个词让政治借用了月亮的节律。

abstract.en: Tide is change that comes back: rise, fall, rise again.
abstract.cn: tide 是会回来的变化：涨、落、再涨。

examples.en: We crossed the causeway at low tide.
examples.cn: 我们在退潮时穿过了那条堤道。

examples.en: The tide of public opinion has changed.
examples.cn: 公众舆论的潮流已经变了。

examples.en: This money should tide us over until spring.
examples.cn: 这笔钱应该能帮我们撑到春天。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太的」——浪头太大，一涨一退不由人 → tide 潮水

root: 古英语 tīd「时间、季节、时辰」，源自日耳曼词根「划分、延展」；中古英语由 tide of the sea 取得「潮汐」义，时间义保存于 eventide、Yuletide、tidings，后引申为舆论与运势的潮流。

sensesIntro.en: Tide began as time and then became the sea’s own clock, a rhythm later lent to opinion, fortune and to help given in hard times.
sensesIntro.cn: tide 从「时间」出发，成为海自己的钟，这份节律后来被借给舆论、运势，以及困难时的援手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water climbing the sand and then slowly giving it back.
core.cn: 核心意象：海水爬上沙滩，又缓缓把沙还给岸。

branches.en: The sea: twice-daily rise and fall.
branches.cn: 海洋线：一日两度的涨落。

branches.en: The opinion: a current that can turn.
branches.cn: 舆论线：可以转向的水流。

branches.en: The old time sense: eventide, Yuletide.
branches.cn: 旧时间线：eventide、Yuletide。

branches.en: The help: floating someone over a hard stretch.
branches.cn: 援助线：把人浮着渡过难关。

branches.en: Water and politics share one rhythmic image.
branches.cn: 水与政治共用同一个节律意象。

intro.en: Tide takes -al for the adjective and compounds with water.
intro.cn: tide 加 -al 构成形容词，并与 water 复合。

latinIntro.en: The stem is native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 词干为日耳曼本土词，拉丁词条留空。

items.meaning: the rise and fall of the sea
evening, in the old time sense
a flow of water or opinion
